contexts.correctionCheck: Publisher/PubMed records and available correction links checked; no notice resolving the stated inconsistencies was identified. This is not exhaustive correction or replication surveillance.
contexts.finding: Selected microglial or purinergic perturbations altered neural readouts, adenosine assays and seizure susceptibility. A1 agonist rescue depended on the genetic preparation.
limitations: Adult seizure cohorts have conflicting descriptions: Animals gives 8-16 weeks for pharmacological experiments, while Seizure Induction gives 14-20 weeks for all seizure experiments. No exact age is selected from this conflict. Genetic cohorts generally include both sexes; pharmacological seizure cohorts are male.

These are distinct genetic preparations. Cx3cr1-CreERT2 targets a lineage rather than proving absolute microglia specificity; P2ry12 deletion is whole-animal, and Drd1a-Cre ligand/receptor deletions are developmental. Cre-negative littermates are the stated default controls.

Neonatal P5-P7 cultures and adult in vivo preparations remain separate. Figure 4c is extracellular striatal dialysate under isoflurane; Figure 4h is a tissue-homogenate fluorescence assay after D1 agonist.

Cortical bouton imaging and striatal calcium imaging are different preparations. The cortical caption says intraperitoneal CNO/clopidogrel while its Methods says intravenous CNO. The neuronal-imaging virus volume and the A1-antagonist dose units also contain unresolved inconsistencies.

Cell and process counts do not replace independent mice. Calcium magnitude and rate-interaction nulls, receptor-specific rescue failures and challenge-specific nulls constrain generalization. Code, raw imaging and all supplementary datasets have not been independently replayed.

Published results and source-table checks are not an independent biological replication. Behavioral stage IV-V seizures are an induced challenge endpoint, not a universal measure of neural stability or a human treatment result.

limitations: Both male and female mice at least seven weeks old were used; exact age and sex distributions per assay group are not supplied. No randomized animal allocation, blinded investigation or prospective statistical sample-size calculation is reported. The reporting summary discusses stimulus ordering separately; it does not establish randomized animal groups.

FOS labeling is an activity-associated marker; Vglut2-cre bulk GCaMP6s is a population calcium signal, not a DBH-specific spike recording. Photometry uses saline on day 4 and LPS on day 5 in the same animals. Vagotomized mice form a separate group after two weeks of recovery; a matched abdominal sham is not explicitly specified in the reviewed procedure. Figure 1c reports residual responses after an approximately 80% reduction.

LPS doses differ across assays: 50 micrograms/kg for FOS and TRAP, 0.5 mg/kg for the main photometry comparison, 0.1 mg/kg for cytokine chemogenetics and 12.5 mg/kg for survival. These exposures are not interchangeable. LPS endotoxaemia is distinct from viable bacterial infection.

Fos-based TRAP2 labeling is followed by at least four weeks before functional rechallenge to restore LPS sensitivity. LPS-TRAPed, Dbh-cre, Vglut2-cre and Vgat-cre populations are not identical. Dbh expression does not measure norepinephrine release or identify a unique molecular mediator.

For standard cytokine chemogenetics, Methods specify CNO at 2 mg/kg twelve hours and 1 mg/kg one hour before challenge; schematics and captions show only the one-hour pretreatment. mCherry controls receive CNO. Saline/LPS tests use the same cohort at least seven days apart, whereas hM3Dq/hM4Di versus mCherry comparisons use separate groups. Blood ELISA at two hours does not identify cytokine-producing cells.

Extended Data 8e shows two IL-10/fat co-responders among 63 neurons, which the authors did not consider further. Universal zero overlap is unsupported.

Injected cytokines and extraintestinal perfusion have different doses, routes and recording windows. The response classifier uses baseline median absolute deviation, a mean modified z-score above 1.6 and peak fluorescence of at least 1%. Selected, normalized responder heatmaps are not an unbiased full-population distribution. In vivo responses do not establish direct cytokine binding to a neuronal receptor; epithelial or immune intermediates remain possible. Referenced imaging procedures have not been fully audited.

Survival experiments use separate Trpa1-cre nodose and Dbh-cre cNST cohorts after high-dose LPS, with repeated 5 mg/kg CNO dosing. Figure 6 shows survival through nine days, not a lifelong or clinical outcome. Separate infection experiments use oral Salmonella and eight CNO injections beginning twelve hours before inoculation; bacterial load is measured in spleen and mesenteric lymph nodes at day five.

Nonsignificance is not equivalence or proof of no pathway contribution. The corticosterone null is a two-hour circulating concentration, not complete exclusion of hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal mediation. Extended Data 3 reuses the Figure 2c saline/LPS data; it is not an independent replication.

The cNST transcriptomic atlas pools tissue from five animals; 4,008 cells and expression clusters are not independent animal replicates, anatomical coordinates or a measured connectome. Rabies labeling supports an anatomical input interpretation, not synaptic efficacy. Main text calls the rabies reporter dsRed while Methods and Extended Data 12 specify GFP; panel 12d depicts Trpa1 but repeats Calca in its quantitative caption. No tracing fraction is calibrated.

Descending efferent routes and immune effector cells remain unresolved. A whole-animal Myd88 knockout does not isolate immune-cell-specific mediation. Lower circulating inflammatory cytokines do not imply universally better defense: sustained TRPA1-population activation increased Salmonella tissue burden in the separate live-infection assay.

Raw measurements, animal identifiers and custom code have not been obtained or replayed. Exclusion criteria include unsuccessful targeting/expression/ablation, but counts and operational thresholds are incomplete. Extended Data 9c reports Gpr65 IL-6 P=0.03 despite a broad no-appreciable-effect conclusion; its small plotted decrease must not be turned into an all-population null. No numerical edge weight or universal carrier count is assigned.

The DSS Methods specify CNO in the experimental cohort drinking solution, while Figure 6 says all animals received CNO. Matched control exposure and intake need resolution before a selective DSS mechanism is admitted. This issue does not change the separately described injected-CNO LPS or infection protocols.

contexts.correctionCheck: Publisher/PMC metadata and exact-DOI correction searches checked on 13 September 2026; no resolving notice was identified. This is not exhaustive notice surveillance. Published online 3 April 2011; issue dated 28 April 2011.
contexts.finding: The Bax manipulation increases surviving cell labels and selected LTP and behavioral responses. It supports task-specific intervention effects, while unique mediation by neuron number and irradiation-based cognitive necessity remain unresolved.
limitations: NCff mice carry Nestin-CreERT2 and two floxed Bax alleles on a mixed C57BL/6-129/SvEv background. The primary contrast is tamoxifen versus vehicle within NCff, starting at at least eight weeks. Reporter NCY versus NCffY comparisons use separate littermate groups both receiving tamoxifen; Cre-negative Bax-floxed controls are another comparison.

The manipulation reduces Bax-dependent cell death in the Nestin stem/progenitor lineage; it is not a selective increase in birth rate or a dentate-newborn-neuron-only intervention. Olfactory-bulb survival also changes. Reporter recombination is a proxy, and altered cell properties or other lineage effects remain alternative mediators.

Behavioral testing is generally at 14-18 weeks with both sexes, but fear conditioning, discrimination, extinction and clearance use males. Experiments and analyses were blinded to genotype or treatment. A complete randomized allocation, exclusion, cage and prospective sample-size manifest is not reported.

The eight-week dentate BrdU assay labels on days 9-18 and counts on day 56; only a subset is NeuN-positive. Counts, marker fractions, proliferation and mature output are distinct. The olfactory and running BrdU schedules differ. Reporter neuron counts per section are not whole-dentate totals.

Weak-tetanus LTP is a population field response, not a birthdated single-cell recording. Eight-week assays without bicuculline use eight slices/six vehicle mice and eleven slices/seven tamoxifen mice; with bicuculline they use four slices/three vehicle and six slices/three tamoxifen mice. Slice-level statistics do not reconstruct animal-level independence.

Main Figure 2c alternates the order of contexts across days, whereas the discrimination Methods describe training context A followed one hour later by similar context B. The exact per-animal schedule requires reconciliation. The nine-day ratio analysis reports treatment P=0.023; its day F/degree-of-freedom/P combination also needs correction. Handling of a zero sum of freezing scores is unspecified.

Contextual freezing discrimination is a behavioral proxy for pattern separation, not a direct measurement of DG neural population codes or general memory improvement. Supplementary protocol variants have treatment P=0.38 and P=0.06 despite interactions or day-specific differences; they cannot be pooled as uniformly positive main effects.

Irradiation uses separate ten-week-old Bax-floxed mice and three 5 Gy exposures on days 1, 4 and 8, with behavior four months later. Regional irradiation is not a selective newborn-neuron ablation or a rescue experiment. Recall samples are eight sham/nine irradiated mice, versus seven/nine in discrimination; the missing sham inclusion is unresolved.

Supplementary Figure 14 reports an overall discrimination-ratio treatment P=0.1 and interaction P=0.3. Late within-group differences are not a between-group necessity test. Its day-five F(1,14)=4.34/P=0.04 pair needs reconciliation; no replacement biological P value is calculated here.

Running is a shared-cage exposure: two wheels for four to five mice, beginning five weeks after treatment. Figure 4 shows behavior on days 64-84. Individual running dose and cage independence are unresolved. Increased locomotion complicates an isolated anxiety interpretation, and home-cage activity has a separate sample.

Supplementary Figure 18 contains invalid negative F notation and conflicting novelty-suppressed-feeding significance; Figure 19 has a control-label conflict. contexts.correctionCheck: Publisher and PubMed metadata and exact-DOI correction searches checked. DOI 10.1038/nn.4542 is a commentary, not an erratum. No identified correction resolves the listed reporting conflicts; this is not exhaustive notice surveillance.
contexts.finding: Capillary potassium evokes upstream dilation and hyperpolarization and increased RBC passage under specified conditions. Endothelial Kcnj2 deletion reduces the whisker perfusion response without eliminating it.
limitations: Adult male mice; Online Methods state two to three months, but Supplementary Table 2 reports mean ages of 14.8 weeks for C57BL/6 and 17.0 weeks for knockout laser-Doppler cohorts. No exact universal age range is admitted. No randomization, blinding, prospective sample-size calculation or exclusions were reported.

Kcnj2 deletion uses constitutive Tek-Cre, not adult-induced capillary-only deletion. Isolated cEC currents and control smooth-muscle currents support endothelial attribution but do not exclude developmental effects or establish restriction to one vascular segment. Identical listed genotyping primer pairs require verification before protocol reproduction.

Whole-cell currents are measured with 60 mM external potassium; this recording solution is distinct from 10 mM focal capillary stimulation, 15 mM cortical superfusion and physiological neural release. Kir2.1/Kcnj2 is the primary molecular identity. Ba2+ also blocks vascular Kir channels outside capillary endothelium.

CaPA is an isolated, pressurized preparation with sealed capillary ends, not normal flowing blood. Diameter, upstream smooth-muscle voltage and in vivo flux come from separate recordings. Membrane-potential recordings use wortmannin to suppress movement. Estimated conduction speed is inferred from distance and onset, not voltage measured along every endothelial cell.

In vivo measurements use acute cranial windows and alpha-chloralose/urethane after isoflurane surgery. RBC flux is cells per second; velocity is distance per time; laser Doppler gives a relative tissue perfusion signal. None is BOLD, oxygen consumption or an exact anatomical network reconstruction.

contexts.correctionCheck: Publisher and PubMed metadata and exact-DOI correction searches checked. DOI 10.1038/nn.4542 is a commentary, not an erratum. No identified correction resolves the listed reporting conflicts; this is not exhaustive notice surveillance.
contexts.finding: Capillary potassium evokes upstream dilation and hyperpolarization and increased RBC passage under specified conditions. Endothelial Kcnj2 deletion reduces the whisker perfusion response without eliminating it.
limitations: Adult male mice; Online Methods state two to three months, but Supplementary Table 2 reports mean ages of 14.8 weeks for C57BL/6 and 17.0 weeks for knockout laser-Doppler cohorts. No exact universal age range is admitted. No randomization, blinding, prospective sample-size calculation or exclusions were reported.

Kcnj2 deletion uses constitutive Tek-Cre, not adult-induced capillary-only deletion. Isolated cEC currents and control smooth-muscle currents support endothelial attribution but do not exclude developmental effects or establish restriction to one vascular segment. Identical listed genotyping primer pairs require verification before protocol reproduction.

Whole-cell currents are measured with 60 mM external potassium; this recording solution is distinct from 10 mM focal capillary stimulation, 15 mM cortical superfusion and physiological neural release. Kir2.1/Kcnj2 is the primary molecular identity. Ba2+ also blocks vascular Kir channels outside capillary endothelium.

CaPA is an isolated, pressurized preparation with sealed capillary ends, not normal flowing blood. Diameter, upstream smooth-muscle voltage and in vivo flux come from separate recordings. Membrane-potential recordings use wortmannin to suppress movement. Estimated conduction speed is inferred from distance and onset, not voltage measured along every endothelial cell.

In vivo measurements use acute cranial windows and alpha-chloralose/urethane after isoflurane surgery. RBC flux is cells per second; velocity is distance per time; laser Doppler gives a relative tissue perfusion signal. None is BOLD, oxygen consumption or an exact anatomical network reconstruction.

Peak RBC flux is the maximum one-second bin in an approximately seventeen-second post-stimulus interval relative to about three seconds of baseline. Velocity is sampled in the peak-flux bin, not an independently selected peak. Paired observations and nested capillaries are not independent mice.

The Figure 4 diameter null concerns eighteen capillaries in seven mice; the authors state that sampled measurement sites lacked pericytes. Upstream diameter uses eight paired experiments in seven mice. The local null does not exclude pericyte effects at other segments or prove equivalence.

Whisker responses persist after endothelial Kcnj2 deletion. Surface barium has a broader target range and leaves residual perfusion responses. The potassium source during neural activity and the complete intercellular route remain unresolved; potassium ejection bypasses the physiological release step.

Supplementary Figure 5 reports five preparations but paired t statistics with five degrees of freedom; Figure 7 reports group sizes inconsistent with its unpaired-test degrees of freedom. Supplementary Table 1 and Table 2 also reverse control-line sample counts for the flow comparisons. Exact quantitative calibration requires animal-identified measurements and resolution.

Nonsignificance is not equivalence. The selected SK/IK activation protocols do not exclude every calcium-dependent endothelial channel. The LFP control tests selected spectral bands, not complete neural activity, and the TTX potassium experiment does not identify the physiological potassium-releasing cell.

Raw recordings and custom MATLAB LFP software have not been obtained or reproduced. The reporting checklist and main text do not provide a resolved access route. No numerical edge weights, universal minimal carrier counts or independently validated full pathway are assigned.

Field plasticity uses different P20-25 slices at 30 C and a single 1 s, 100 Hz train. Early PTP/STP and late 30-45 min LTP have separate outcomes; altered potassium handling is not isolated from altered glutamate handling or development.

Sex and animal-level clustering of the selected electrophysiological samples are not established in this reading. Published nulls are not equivalence tests, and no raw-recording reproduction is claimed.

contexts.correctionCheck: Author-lab PDF, PubMed/Europe PMC metadata and exact DOI correction, erratum and retraction searches were checked on 14 September 2026. Metadata links comments with DOIs 10.1038/6300 and 10.1038/s41593-018-0214-1; these are commentary, not identified corrections. No notice resolving the printed statistical conflicts was identified; this is not exhaustive surveillance.
contexts.finding: Trace and place protocols increase previously labeled dentate-cell counts and reduce total pyknotic profiles. Other tasks and late-label counts retain null outcomes. Survival and functional necessity remain distinct mechanistic questions.
limitations: Adult male Sprague Dawley rats weighed 300-350 g; chronological age is not stated. Group sizes are generally five or six. The paper does not provide a complete animal manifest or randomized assignment procedure. Coded histology is reported, not complete blinding of every procedure.

BrdU was 200 mg/kg; the injection route is not specified. In the main experiments labeling occurred one week before four consecutive training days, with separate terminal cohorts 24 hours or seven days after training. The approximate three-week label-age wording does not exactly specify elapsed days. Separate sacrificed cohorts do not track individual cells longitudinally.

Trace conditioning used 200 trials per day for four days, an 83-dB 250-ms noise, a 500-ms gap and a 100-ms 0.7-mA shock. Unpaired rats received the same stimulus counts without explicit pairing. All paired animals reached 60% conditioned responses; none of the unpaired animals did. Complete naive-group electrode and handling matching is not specified.

Delay conditioning uses a 320-ms noise coterminating with an 80-ms shock and a different conditioned-response window. Trace and delay differ in stimulus durations and scoring as well as temporal gap. The reported F(1,19)=4.24, P=0.05 is called nonsignificant; this boundary result and final-day similarity are not statistical equivalence.

Place training uses a fixed submerged platform, cue training a visible platform moved among quadrants, with four trials per day for four days. Swim controls are yoked to place-training swim duration without a platform; their interval includes the omitted platform-rest time. Time matching does not establish identical stress, motivation or hormone exposure.

Hippocampal dependence is imported from prior lesion literature and, for the exact rat trace protocol, unpublished lesion data. No matched hippocampal lesion or selective newborn-cell manipulation is performed in this histology study. The graph links the specified task protocol to its measured outcome, not generic hippocampal necessity.

At 24 hours after training, prelabelled dentate BrdU counts are elevated after trace conditioning (F(2,15)=137.40, P=0.0001) and place training (F(3,20)=266.40, P=0.0001); Figure 1b/f gives six rats per group. Exact endpoint means are not tabulated and have not been digitized. The abstract doubling language is not an exact universal multiplier or an edge weight.

Delay conditioning has no detected BrdU-count increase (F(2,12)=1.889, P=0.1936); cue training and time-yoked swimming also lack the reported place-training increase. Nonsignificance is neither equivalence nor absence of a smaller effect. These selected tasks and controls do not prove that all possible learning or stress is irrelevant.

The late-labeling trace cohort receives BrdU on the final training day after learning criterion, followed by tissue collection 24 hours later. F(2,13)=0.011, P=0.9892 concerns that retained-label count, not every phase of proliferation throughout training or a direct instantaneous mitotic rate.

Subgranular pyknotic profiles are defined morphologically, not by neuron-specific birthdated identity. Trace means are 220.0 +/- 41.9 naive, 81.8 +/- 24.3 paired and 214.8 +/- 46.5 unpaired; the printed F(3,15)=12.339, P=0.0007 gives a numerator degree of freedom inconsistent with three ordinary ANOVA groups. No corrected statistic is substituted.

Place-training pyknotic means are 208.7 +/- 30.9 naive, 50.0 +/- 8.4 place, 222.0 +/- 48.1 cue and 236.0 +/- 34.2 swim, with reported F(3,20)=16.527, P=0.0001. The paragraph does not allocate these pyknotic counts unambiguously to the 24-hour or seven-day terminal cohorts. Reduced total pyknosis does not by itself identify survival of the BrdU-positive neuronal population.

BrdU-positive pyknotic profiles are rare, reported as 0-36 per dentate gyrus, and not observed after the two selected learning tasks. No BrdU-positive pyknotic profiles are observed in the 24-hour late-labeling cohort. These are detection-limited snapshots of labeled degeneration, not complete survival trajectories.

SVZ sampling excludes the anterior portion and uses sections spanning the dentate gyrus. The trace SVZ null is printed as F(2,15)=0.09 with P=0.3598, an inconsistent ordinary F-test pair. The maze SVZ null is F(3,20)=0.279, P=0.8538. Neither result establishes absence throughout the SVZ or brain.

Granule-cell-layer volume has no detected group difference in trace (F(2,15)=0.043, P=0.958) or maze (F(3,20)=0.302, P=0.8236) comparisons. Gross regional volume is not the count of newborn neurons, a measured replacement balance or an equivalence test.

The seven-day post-training groups are reported to retain elevated BrdU counts, without a separate endpoint figure, table or test. Marker proportions at that endpoint are approximately 57% TOAD-64, 11% GFAP and 71% calbindin among BrdU-labeled cells. Separate overlapping marker assays must not be summed into a cell-type partition.

Marker comparisons report F(3,20)=0.311, P=0.8169 for TOAD-64 and identical F(3,20)=0.572, P=0.6402 for GFAP and calbindin. Exact assay/cohort allocation and the duplicated statistics require raw data; they are not silently repaired. Minimum sampling is 50 labeled cells per animal on at least six sections, with confocal verification.

Counts use coded slides, every twelfth 40-micrometre coronal section and exclusion of the outermost focal plane. Pyknotic counts use the same modified optical fractionator; volume uses Cavalieri estimation. Processed thickness, raw counts, optical stacks and analysis code are unavailable. Statistical methods specify Neuman Keuls comparisons.

The control time course rises from two hours to one week and falls by two weeks after labeling, but involves separate terminal cohorts. The survival interpretation also draws on prior autoradiographic grain counts and unpublished observations. The authors explicitly cannot exclude proliferation; a unique survival mechanism is not experimentally isolated.

No newborn-cell necessity, selective rescue, synaptic-output or memory-storage test is performed. Untrained controls retain labeled cells, and the authors leave unspecified natural learning as a possible contributor to baseline survival. The study establishes neither a universal learning prerequisite nor its universal absence, and no primate or human generalization follows.

All six pages of main scientific text, Methods and figure captions were read in the author-lab PDF; all panels of Figures 1-2 and the printed statistical passages on pages 261-262 were visually inspected. Animal-level data, raw images and analysis code were not obtained or reproduced.

contexts.finding: Trace and place protocols increase previously labeled dentate-cell counts and reduce total pyknotic profiles. Other tasks and late-label counts retain null outcomes. Survival and functional necessity remain distinct mechanistic questions.
limitations: Adult male Sprague Dawley rats weighed 300-350 g; chronological age is not stated. Group sizes are generally five or six. The paper does not provide a complete animal manifest or randomized assignment procedure. Coded histology is reported, not complete blinding of every procedure.

BrdU was 200 mg/kg; the injection route is not specified. In the main experiments labeling occurred one week before four consecutive training days, with separate terminal cohorts 24 hours or seven days after training. The approximate three-week label-age wording does not exactly specify elapsed days. Separate sacrificed cohorts do not track individual cells longitudinally.

Trace conditioning used 200 trials per day for four days, an 83-dB 250-ms noise, a 500-ms gap and a 100-ms 0.7-mA shock. Unpaired rats received the same stimulus counts without explicit pairing. All paired animals reached 60% conditioned responses; none of the unpaired animals did. Complete naive-group electrode and handling matching is not specified.

Delay conditioning uses a 320-ms noise coterminating with an 80-ms shock and a different conditioned-response window. Trace and delay differ in stimulus durations and scoring as well as temporal gap. The reported F(1,19)=4.24, P=0.05 is called nonsignificant; this boundary result and final-day similarity are not statistical equivalence.

Place training uses a fixed submerged platform, cue training a visible platform moved among quadrants, with four trials per day for four days. Swim controls are yoked to place-training swim duration without a platform; their interval includes the omitted platform-rest time. Time matching does not establish identical stress, motivation or hormone exposure.

Hippocampal dependence is imported from prior lesion literature and, for the exact rat trace protocol, unpublished lesion data. No matched hippocampal lesion or selective newborn-cell manipulation is performed in this histology study. The graph links the specified task protocol to its measured outcome, not generic hippocampal necessity.

At 24 hours after training, prelabelled dentate BrdU counts are elevated after trace conditioning (F(2,15)=137.40, P=0.0001) and place training (F(3,20)=266.40, P=0.0001); Figure 1b/f gives six rats per group. Exact endpoint means are not tabulated and have not been digitized. The abstract doubling language is not an exact universal multiplier or an edge weight.

Delay conditioning has no detected BrdU-count increase (F(2,12)=1.889, P=0.1936); cue training and time-yoked swimming also lack the reported place-training increase. Nonsignificance is neither equivalence nor absence of a smaller effect. These selected tasks and controls do not prove that all possible learning or stress is irrelevant.

The late-labeling trace cohort receives BrdU on the final training day after learning criterion, followed by tissue collection 24 hours later. F(2,13)=0.011, P=0.9892 concerns that retained-label count, not every phase of proliferation throughout training or a direct instantaneous mitotic rate.

Subgranular pyknotic profiles are defined morphologically, not by neuron-specific birthdated identity. Trace means are 220.0 +/- 41.9 naive, 81.8 +/- 24.3 paired and 214.8 +/- 46.5 unpaired; the printed F(3,15)=12.339, P=0.0007 gives a numerator degree of freedom inconsistent with three ordinary ANOVA groups. No corrected statistic is substituted.

Place-training pyknotic means are 208.7 +/- 30.9 naive, 50.0 +/- 8.4 place, 222.0 +/- 48.1 cue and 236.0 +/- 34.2 swim, with reported F(3,20)=16.527, P=0.0001. The paragraph does not allocate these pyknotic counts unambiguously to the 24-hour or seven-day terminal cohorts. Reduced total pyknosis does not by itself identify survival of the BrdU-positive neuronal population.

BrdU-positive pyknotic profiles are rare, reported as 0-36 per dentate gyrus, and not observed after the two selected learning tasks. No BrdU-positive pyknotic profiles are observed in the 24-hour late-labeling cohort. These are detection-limited snapshots of labeled degeneration, not complete survival trajectories.

SVZ sampling excludes the anterior portion and uses sections spanning the dentate gyrus. The trace SVZ null is printed as F(2,15)=0.09 with P=0.3598, an inconsistent ordinary F-test pair. The maze SVZ null is F(3,20)=0.279, P=0.8538. Neither result establishes absence throughout the SVZ or brain.

Granule-cell-layer volume has no detected group difference in trace (F(2,15)=0.043, P=0.958) or maze (F(3,20)=0.302, P=0.8236) comparisons. Gross regional volume is not the count of newborn neurons, a measured replacement balance or an equivalence test.

The seven-day post-training groups are reported to retain elevated BrdU counts, without a separate endpoint figure, table or test. Marker proportions at that endpoint are approximately 57% TOAD-64, 11% GFAP and 71% calbindin among BrdU-labeled cells. Separate overlapping marker assays must not be summed into a cell-type partition.

Marker comparisons report F(3,20)=0.311, P=0.8169 for TOAD-64 and identical F(3,20)=0.572, P=0.6402 for GFAP and calbindin. Exact assay/cohort allocation and the duplicated statistics require raw data; they are not silently repaired. Minimum sampling is 50 labeled cells per animal on at least six sections, with confocal verification.

Counts use coded slides, every twelfth 40-micrometre coronal section and exclusion of the outermost focal plane. Pyknotic counts use the same modified optical fractionator; volume uses Cavalieri estimation. Processed thickness, raw counts, optical stacks and analysis code are unavailable. Statistical methods specify Neuman Keuls comparisons.

The control time course rises from two hours to one week and falls by two weeks after labeling, but involves separate terminal cohorts. The survival interpretation also draws on prior autoradiographic grain counts and unpublished observations. The authors explicitly cannot exclude proliferation; a unique survival mechanism is not experimentally isolated.

No newborn-cell necessity, selective rescue, synaptic-output or memory-storage test is performed. Untrained controls retain labeled cells, and the authors leave unspecified natural learning as a possible contributor to baseline survival. The study establishes neither a universal learning prerequisite nor its universal absence, and no primate or human generalization follows.

contexts.finding: Trace and place protocols increase previously labeled dentate-cell counts and reduce total pyknotic profiles. Other tasks and late-label counts retain null outcomes. Survival and functional necessity remain distinct mechanistic questions.
limitations: Adult male Sprague Dawley rats weighed 300-350 g; chronological age is not stated. Group sizes are generally five or six. The paper does not provide a complete animal manifest or randomized assignment procedure. Coded histology is reported, not complete blinding of every procedure.

BrdU was 200 mg/kg; the injection route is not specified. In the main experiments labeling occurred one week before four consecutive training days, with separate terminal cohorts 24 hours or seven days after training. The approximate three-week label-age wording does not exactly specify elapsed days. Separate sacrificed cohorts do not track individual cells longitudinally.

Trace conditioning used 200 trials per day for four days, an 83-dB 250-ms noise, a 500-ms gap and a 100-ms 0.7-mA shock. Unpaired rats received the same stimulus counts without explicit pairing. All paired animals reached 60% conditioned responses; none of the unpaired animals did. Complete naive-group electrode and handling matching is not specified.

Delay conditioning uses a 320-ms noise coterminating with an 80-ms shock and a different conditioned-response window. Trace and delay differ in stimulus durations and scoring as well as temporal gap. The reported F(1,19)=4.24, P=0.05 is called nonsignificant; this boundary result and final-day similarity are not statistical equivalence.

Place training uses a fixed submerged platform, cue training a visible platform moved among quadrants, with four trials per day for four days. Swim controls are yoked to place-training swim duration without a platform; their interval includes the omitted platform-rest time. Time matching does not establish identical stress, motivation or hormone exposure.

Hippocampal dependence is imported from prior lesion literature and, for the exact rat trace protocol, unpublished lesion data. No matched hippocampal lesion or selective newborn-cell manipulation is performed in this histology study. The graph links the specified task protocol to its measured outcome, not generic hippocampal necessity.

At 24 hours after training, prelabelled dentate BrdU counts are elevated after trace conditioning (F(2,15)=137.40, P=0.0001) and place training (F(3,20)=266.40, P=0.0001); Figure 1b/f gives six rats per group. Exact endpoint means are not tabulated and have not been digitized. The abstract doubling language is not an exact universal multiplier or an edge weight.

Delay conditioning has no detected BrdU-count increase (F(2,12)=1.889, P=0.1936); cue training and time-yoked swimming also lack the reported place-training increase. Nonsignificance is neither equivalence nor absence of a smaller effect. These selected tasks and controls do not prove that all possible learning or stress is irrelevant.

The late-labeling trace cohort receives BrdU on the final training day after learning criterion, followed by tissue collection 24 hours later. F(2,13)=0.011, P=0.9892 concerns that retained-label count, not every phase of proliferation throughout training or a direct instantaneous mitotic rate.

Subgranular pyknotic profiles are defined morphologically, not by neuron-specific birthdated identity. Trace means are 220.0 +/- 41.9 naive, 81.8 +/- 24.3 paired and 214.8 +/- 46.5 unpaired; the printed F(3,15)=12.339, P=0.0007 gives a numerator degree of freedom inconsistent with three ordinary ANOVA groups. No corrected statistic is substituted.

Place-training pyknotic means are 208.7 +/- 30.9 naive, 50.0 +/- 8.4 place, 222.0 +/- 48.1 cue and 236.0 +/- 34.2 swim, with reported F(3,20)=16.527, P=0.0001. The paragraph does not allocate these pyknotic counts unambiguously to the 24-hour or seven-day terminal cohorts. Reduced total pyknosis does not by itself identify survival of the BrdU-positive neuronal population.

BrdU-positive pyknotic profiles are rare, reported as 0-36 per dentate gyrus, and not observed after the two selected learning tasks. No BrdU-positive pyknotic profiles are observed in the 24-hour late-labeling cohort. These are detection-limited snapshots of labeled degeneration, not complete survival trajectories.

SVZ sampling excludes the anterior portion and uses sections spanning the dentate gyrus. The trace SVZ null is printed as F(2,15)=0.09 with P=0.3598, an inconsistent ordinary F-test pair. The maze SVZ null is F(3,20)=0.279, P=0.8538. Neither result establishes absence throughout the SVZ or brain.

Granule-cell-layer volume has no detected group difference in trace (F(2,15)=0.043, P=0.958) or maze (F(3,20)=0.302, P=0.8236) comparisons. Gross regional volume is not the count of newborn neurons, a measured replacement balance or an equivalence test.

The seven-day post-training groups are reported to retain elevated BrdU counts, without a separate endpoint figure, table or test. Marker proportions at that endpoint are approximately 57% TOAD-64, 11% GFAP and 71% calbindin among BrdU-labeled cells. Separate overlapping marker assays must not be summed into a cell-type partition.

Marker comparisons report F(3,20)=0.311, P=0.8169 for TOAD-64 and identical F(3,20)=0.572, P=0.6402 for GFAP and calbindin. Exact assay/cohort allocation and the duplicated statistics require raw data; they are not silently repaired. Minimum sampling is 50 labeled cells per animal on at least six sections, with confocal verification.

Counts use coded slides, every twelfth 40-micrometre coronal section and exclusion of the outermost focal plane. Pyknotic counts use the same modified optical fractionator; volume uses Cavalieri estimation. Processed thickness, raw counts, optical stacks and analysis code are unavailable. Statistical methods specify Neuman Keuls comparisons.

The control time course rises from two hours to one week and falls by two weeks after labeling, but involves separate terminal cohorts. The survival interpretation also draws on prior autoradiographic grain counts and unpublished observations. The authors explicitly cannot exclude proliferation; a unique survival mechanism is not experimentally isolated.

No newborn-cell necessity, selective rescue, synaptic-output or memory-storage test is performed. Untrained controls retain labeled cells, and the authors leave unspecified natural learning as a possible contributor to baseline survival. The study establishes neither a universal learning prerequisite nor its universal absence, and no primate or human generalization follows.

All six pages of main scientific text, Methods and figure captions were read in the author-lab PDF; all panels of Figures 1-2 and the printed statistical passages on pages 261-262 were visually inspected. Animal-level data, raw images and analysis code were not obtained or reproduced.

Trace conditioning used 200 trials per day for four days, an 83-dB 250-ms noise, a 500-ms gap and a 100-ms 0.7-mA shock. Unpaired rats received the same stimulus counts without explicit pairing. All paired animals reached 60% conditioned responses; none of the unpaired animals did. Complete naive-group electrode and handling matching is not specified.

Delay conditioning uses a 320-ms noise coterminating with an 80-ms shock and a different conditioned-response window. Trace and delay differ in stimulus durations and scoring as well as temporal gap. The reported F(1,19)=4.24, P=0.05 is called nonsignificant; this boundary result and final-day similarity are not statistical equivalence.

Place training uses a fixed submerged platform, cue training a visible platform moved among quadrants, with four trials per day for four days. Swim controls are yoked to place-training swim duration without a platform; their interval includes the omitted platform-rest time. Time matching does not establish identical stress, motivation or hormone exposure.

Hippocampal dependence is imported from prior lesion literature and, for the exact rat trace protocol, unpublished lesion data. No matched hippocampal lesion or selective newborn-cell manipulation is performed in this histology study. The graph links the specified task protocol to its measured outcome, not generic hippocampal necessity.

At 24 hours after training, prelabelled dentate BrdU counts are elevated after trace conditioning (F(2,15)=137.40, P=0.0001) and place training (F(3,20)=266.40, P=0.0001); Figure 1b/f gives six rats per group. Exact endpoint means are not tabulated and have not been digitized. The abstract doubling language is not an exact universal multiplier or an edge weight.

Delay conditioning has no detected BrdU-count increase (F(2,12)=1.889, P=0.1936); cue training and time-yoked swimming also lack the reported place-training increase. Nonsignificance is neither equivalence nor absence of a smaller effect. These selected tasks and controls do not prove that all possible learning or stress is irrelevant.

The late-labeling trace cohort receives BrdU on the final training day after learning criterion, followed by tissue collection 24 hours later. F(2,13)=0.011, P=0.9892 concerns that retained-label count, not every phase of proliferation throughout training or a direct instantaneous mitotic rate.

Subgranular pyknotic profiles are defined morphologically, not by neuron-specific birthdated identity. Trace means are 220.0 +/- 41.9 naive, 81.8 +/- 24.3 paired and 214.8 +/- 46.5 unpaired; the printed F(3,15)=12.339, P=0.0007 gives a numerator degree of freedom inconsistent with three ordinary ANOVA groups. No corrected statistic is substituted.

Place-training pyknotic means are 208.7 +/- 30.9 naive, 50.0 +/- 8.4 place, 222.0 +/- 48.1 cue and 236.0 +/- 34.2 swim, with reported F(3,20)=16.527, P=0.0001. The paragraph does not allocate these pyknotic counts unambiguously to the 24-hour or seven-day terminal cohorts. Reduced total pyknosis does not by itself identify survival of the BrdU-positive neuronal population.

BrdU-positive pyknotic profiles are rare, reported as 0-36 per dentate gyrus, and not observed after the two selected learning tasks. No BrdU-positive pyknotic profiles are observed in the 24-hour late-labeling cohort. These are detection-limited snapshots of labeled degeneration, not complete survival trajectories.

SVZ sampling excludes the anterior portion and uses sections spanning the dentate gyrus. The trace SVZ null is printed as F(2,15)=0.09 with P=0.3598, an inconsistent ordinary F-test pair. The maze SVZ null is F(3,20)=0.279, P=0.8538. Neither result establishes absence throughout the SVZ or brain.

Granule-cell-layer volume has no detected group difference in trace (F(2,15)=0.043, P=0.958) or maze (F(3,20)=0.302, P=0.8236) comparisons. Gross regional volume is not the count of newborn neurons, a measured replacement balance or an equivalence test.

The seven-day post-training groups are reported to retain elevated BrdU counts, without a separate endpoint figure, table or test. Marker proportions at that endpoint are approximately 57% TOAD-64, 11% GFAP and 71% calbindin among BrdU-labeled cells. Separate overlapping marker assays must not be summed into a cell-type partition.

Marker comparisons report F(3,20)=0.311, P=0.8169 for TOAD-64 and identical F(3,20)=0.572, P=0.6402 for GFAP and calbindin. Exact assay/cohort allocation and the duplicated statistics require raw data; they are not silently repaired. Minimum sampling is 50 labeled cells per animal on at least six sections, with confocal verification.

Counts use coded slides, every twelfth 40-micrometre coronal section and exclusion of the outermost focal plane. Pyknotic counts use the same modified optical fractionator; volume uses Cavalieri estimation. Processed thickness, raw counts, optical stacks and analysis code are unavailable. Statistical methods specify Neuman Keuls comparisons.

The control time course rises from two hours to one week and falls by two weeks after labeling, but involves separate terminal cohorts. The survival interpretation also draws on prior autoradiographic grain counts and unpublished observations. The authors explicitly cannot exclude proliferation; a unique survival mechanism is not experimentally isolated.

No newborn-cell necessity, selective rescue, synaptic-output or memory-storage test is performed. Untrained controls retain labeled cells, and the authors leave unspecified natural learning as a possible contributor to baseline survival. The study establishes neither a universal learning prerequisite nor its universal absence, and no primate or human generalization follows.

All six pages of main scientific text, Methods and figure captions were read in the author-lab PDF; all panels of Figures 1-2 and the printed statistical passages on pages 261-262 were visually inspected. Animal-level data, raw images and analysis code were not obtained or reproduced.

contexts.correctionCheck: Publisher and PubMed records and exact-title notice searches checked. No identified notice resolves the specified method, control or label issues; this is not exhaustive correction or replication surveillance.
contexts.finding: Peripheral challenges evoked neural readouts, while selected neural manipulations changed circulating cytokines. Activation improved high-dose endotoxin survival but increased bacterial tissue load in a different live-infection protocol. A complete descending immune circuit is not identified.
limitations: Both male and female mice at least seven weeks old were used; exact age and sex distributions per assay group are not supplied. No randomized animal allocation, blinded investigation or prospective statistical sample-size calculation is reported. The reporting summary discusses stimulus ordering separately; it does not establish randomized animal groups.

FOS labeling is an activity-associated marker; Vglut2-cre bulk GCaMP6s is a population calcium signal, not a DBH-specific spike recording. Photometry uses saline on day 4 and LPS on day 5 in the same animals. Vagotomized mice form a separate group after two weeks of recovery; a matched abdominal sham is not explicitly specified in the reviewed procedure. Figure 1c reports residual responses after an approximately 80% reduction.

LPS doses differ across assays: 50 micrograms/kg for FOS and TRAP, 0.5 mg/kg for the main photometry comparison, 0.1 mg/kg for cytokine chemogenetics and 12.5 mg/kg for survival. These exposures are not interchangeable. LPS endotoxaemia is distinct from viable bacterial infection.

Fos-based TRAP2 labeling is followed by at least four weeks before functional rechallenge to restore LPS sensitivity. LPS-TRAPed, Dbh-cre, Vglut2-cre and Vgat-cre populations are not identical. Dbh expression does not measure norepinephrine release or identify a unique molecular mediator.

For standard cytokine chemogenetics, Methods specify CNO at 2 mg/kg twelve hours and 1 mg/kg one hour before challenge; schematics and captions show only the one-hour pretreatment. mCherry controls receive CNO. Saline/LPS tests use the same cohort at least seven days apart, whereas hM3Dq/hM4Di versus mCherry comparisons use separate groups. Blood ELISA at two hours does not identify cytokine-producing cells.

Cre-defined nodose activation perturbs marker-defined neurons; it is not selective activation of the TRPA1 channel or CALCA peptide. TRPA1 neurons include different stimulus-responsive subgroups. Extended Data 8e shows two IL-10/fat co-responders among 63 neurons, which the authors did not consider further. Universal zero overlap is unsupported.

Injected cytokines and extraintestinal perfusion have different doses, routes and recording windows. The response classifier uses baseline median absolute deviation, a mean modified z-score above 1.6 and peak fluorescence of at least 1%. Selected, normalized responder heatmaps are not an unbiased full-population distribution. In vivo responses do not establish direct cytokine binding to a neuronal receptor; epithelial or immune intermediates remain possible. Referenced imaging procedures have not been fully audited.

Survival experiments use separate Trpa1-cre nodose and Dbh-cre cNST cohorts after high-dose LPS, with repeated 5 mg/kg CNO dosing. Figure 6 shows survival through nine days, not a lifelong or clinical outcome. Separate infection experiments use oral Salmonella and eight CNO injections beginning twelve hours before inoculation; bacterial load is measured in spleen and mesenteric lymph nodes at day five.

contexts.correctionCheck: Publisher and PubMed records and exact-title notice searches checked. No identified notice resolves the specified method, control or label issues; this is not exhaustive correction or replication surveillance.
contexts.finding: Peripheral challenges evoked neural readouts, while selected neural manipulations changed circulating cytokines. Activation improved high-dose endotoxin survival but increased bacterial tissue load in a different live-infection protocol. A complete descending immune circuit is not identified.
limitations: Both male and female mice at least seven weeks old were used; exact age and sex distributions per assay group are not supplied. No randomized animal allocation, blinded investigation or prospective statistical sample-size calculation is reported. The reporting summary discusses stimulus ordering separately; it does not establish randomized animal groups.

FOS labeling is an activity-associated marker; Vglut2-cre bulk GCaMP6s is a population calcium signal, not a DBH-specific spike recording. Photometry uses saline on day 4 and LPS on day 5 in the same animals. Vagotomized mice form a separate group after two weeks of recovery; a matched abdominal sham is not explicitly specified in the reviewed procedure. Figure 1c reports residual responses after an approximately 80% reduction.

LPS doses differ across assays: 50 micrograms/kg for FOS and TRAP, 0.5 mg/kg for the main photometry comparison, 0.1 mg/kg for cytokine chemogenetics and 12.5 mg/kg for survival. These exposures are not interchangeable. LPS endotoxaemia is distinct from viable bacterial infection.

Fos-based TRAP2 labeling is followed by at least four weeks before functional rechallenge to restore LPS sensitivity. LPS-TRAPed, Dbh-cre, Vglut2-cre and Vgat-cre populations are not identical. Dbh expression does not measure norepinephrine release or identify a unique molecular mediator.

For standard cytokine chemogenetics, Methods specify CNO at 2 mg/kg twelve hours and 1 mg/kg one hour before challenge; schematics and captions show only the one-hour pretreatment. mCherry controls receive CNO. Saline/LPS tests use the same cohort at least seven days apart, whereas hM3Dq/hM4Di versus mCherry comparisons use separate groups. Blood ELISA at two hours does not identify cytokine-producing cells.

Cre-defined nodose activation perturbs marker-defined neurons; it is not selective activation of the TRPA1 channel or CALCA peptide. TRPA1 neurons include different stimulus-responsive subgroups. Extended Data 8e shows two IL-10/fat co-responders among 63 neurons, which the authors did not consider further. Universal zero overlap is unsupported.

Injected cytokines and extraintestinal perfusion have different doses, routes and recording windows. The response classifier uses baseline median absolute deviation, a mean modified z-score above 1.6 and peak fluorescence of at least 1%. Selected, normalized responder heatmaps are not an unbiased full-population distribution. In vivo responses do not establish direct cytokine binding to a neuronal receptor; epithelial or immune intermediates remain possible. Referenced imaging procedures have not been fully audited.

Survival experiments use separate Trpa1-cre nodose and Dbh-cre cNST cohorts after high-dose LPS, with repeated 5 mg/kg CNO dosing. Figure 6 shows survival through nine days, not a lifelong or clinical outcome. Separate infection experiments use oral Salmonella and eight CNO injections beginning twelve hours before inoculation; bacterial load is measured in spleen and mesenteric lymph nodes at day five.

Nonsignificance is not equivalence or proof of no pathway contribution. The corticosterone null is a two-hour circulating concentration, not complete exclusion of hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal mediation. Extended Data 3 reuses the Figure 2c saline/LPS data; it is not an independent replication.

The cNST transcriptomic atlas pools tissue from five animals; 4,008 cells and expression clusters are not independent animal replicates, anatomical coordinates or a measured connectome. Rabies labeling supports an anatomical input interpretation, not synaptic efficacy. Main text calls the rabies reporter dsRed while Methods and Extended Data 12 specify GFP; panel 12d depicts Trpa1 but repeats Calca in its quantitative caption. No tracing fraction is calibrated.

Descending efferent routes and immune effector cells remain unresolved. A whole-animal Myd88 knockout does not isolate immune-cell-specific mediation. Lower circulating inflammatory cytokines do not imply universally better defense: sustained TRPA1-population activation increased Salmonella tissue burden in the separate live-infection assay.

Raw measurements, animal identifiers and custom code have not been obtained or replayed. Exclusion criteria include unsuccessful targeting/expression/ablation, but counts and operational thresholds are incomplete. Extended Data 9c reports Gpr65 IL-6 P=0.03 despite a broad no-appreciable-effect conclusion; its small plotted decrease must not be turned into an all-population null. No numerical edge weight or universal carrier count is assigned.

The DSS Methods specify CNO in the experimental cohort drinking solution, while Figure 6 says all animals received CNO. Matched control exposure and intake need resolution before a selective DSS mechanism is admitted. This issue does not change the separately described injected-CNO LPS or infection protocols.

contexts.correctionCheck: PMC scientific text, PubMed/Europe PMC metadata and exact DOI/title correction, erratum and retraction searches were checked on 14 September 2026. No notice resolving the protocol or allocation questions was identified; this is not exhaustive surveillance.
contexts.finding: The reported marker combinations support adult macaque dentate neuronal and oligodendroglial production under the labeling assumptions. They do not identify a universal rate, common multipotent founder, observed migration, replacement feedback or cognitive function.
contexts.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
limitations: Ten adult macaques of both sexes include Macaca mulatta and Macaca fascicularis, aged 5.5-16.5 years. The paper does not provide an animal-by-species, sex, age, dosing, survival and assay manifest. Ten injected animals do not establish ten independent animals for every neuronal or glial endpoint.

Intravenous BrdU was 50 mg/kg, either once or daily for five consecutive days, administered between 09:00 and noon. Materials and Methods lists survival times ending at 72 days, whereas Results twice gives 75 days as the maximum. The reference injection for that discrepancy is not reconciled; neither value is silently selected.

BrdU and PCNA label DNA synthesis or cell-cycle-associated profiles; they do not continuously observe completed cytokinesis or a clone. PCNA was examined in sections from the same brains, not as a second independent animal cohort or a reported same-cell BrdU/PCNA lineage assay. Apposed doublets suggest, but do not identify, sibling relationships.

Early and later regional labeling is compared across sacrificed animals. BrdU-positive cells at the longest interval are not specifically identified as neurons. Label retention does not establish the survival fraction of a birth cohort, a neuron-specific lifespan, absence of rapid turnover elsewhere or absence of BrdU toxicity.

Neuronal double labeling was examined 32 days after the last of five injections in PFA-fixed 40-micrometre cryosections. Twenty nonadjacent sections were examined for each of NeuN and TuJ1; these are section counts, not independent animals. Exact biological replication, section sampling, denominators and uncertainty are not supplied for the reported averages.

BrdU/NeuN and BrdU/TuJ1 are alternative marker assays, not a reported three-marker identity for every labeled cell. The study reports neuronal colabels in GCL/SGZ and none in the other examined hippocampal regions; sampling and marker sensitivity do not establish absolute regional absence. Raw confocal stacks, optical section positions and segmentation have not been reanalysed.

Fluorophore reversal, omitted-primary controls and Figure 2c-d address staining and channel artifacts. They do not establish lineage, complete specificity or quantified sensitivity. Antibody omission is not a biological no-neurogenesis control, and no matched dose-control experiment establishes BrdU safety.

O4 or CNP double labeling used sequential black nuclear and brown cytoplasmic peroxidase signals in ethanol-fixed paraffin sections of 8 or 10 micrometres. Figure 3 shows 27-day single-injection examples. These preparations are distinct from the 32-day neuronal fluorescence assay; marker-positive morphology does not measure myelin formation or conduction.

Astrocyte generation is attributed to Eckenhoff and Rakic (1988) and Eriksson et al. (1998), not a newly reported GFAP assay in this experiment. Finding several phenotypes near one niche does not establish a shared multipotent founder, self-renewal or exclusive stem-cell lineage. The 1988 GFAP/autoradiographic assays are separately reviewed and do not trace a common founder.

The approximately 1,000 BrdU/TuJ1-positive cells per hippocampus is extrapolated from about two profiles per section, 40-micrometre sections and an approximately 19-mm external anatomical length. Scaling by an external 4.8-million-neuron estimate and dividing by five injections gives the provisional 0.004% per day. This is not a direct daily birth count or an unbiased whole-hippocampus stereological census.

Five-day cumulative labeling followed by 32 days of survival combines labeling opportunity, subsequent division, dilution, survival and marker expression. A single retained-label estimate does not identify production and death separately. The paper itself leaves lower production versus lower survival unresolved. No empirical edge weight or universal rate is assigned.

The roughly tenfold rodent comparison uses a separate published mouse study and external denominators. The paper acknowledges unmatched age, species, environment, labeling and survival procedures. Absolute-age and relative-age hypotheses were not compared in one matched design, and this series supplies no invariant primate-to-human scaling.

Bipolar morphology and radial or tangential orientation support a migration interpretation but do not track displacement, origin or a radial-glial guidance interaction. Nearby cells are not a clone, and anatomical resemblance to developing neurons is not an executed construction rule.

The replacement interpretation draws on separate human neuron counts and macaque synapse counts. Synapse-count stability is not a matched neuron census. This experiment measures neither paired births and deaths, feedback of population state, replacement identity nor the fraction of older neurons ultimately renewed.

No electrical, synaptic-output, learning or memory assay was performed. A possible cognitive role, stable-memory benefit or recovery mechanism remains untested. Labeling in this study does not require an injury or learning manipulation and does not validate the source card's necessary incoming assertions, weights or minimum carrier counts.

All main scientific text, Materials and Methods, and the captions of Figures 1-3 were read in the PMC full text; all three archived figure images were visually inspected. The separate publisher PDF, animal-level manifest, raw histological counts, optical stacks and analysis files were not obtained or independently reproduced.

contexts.finding: Adult CpG site-16 patterns followed foster-care class. TSA altered several molecular readouts and the low-care group stress response, with site-specific and group-specific differences.
limitations: Long-Evans rat hippocampus is bulk tissue containing neurons and glia. High/low licking-grooming and arched-back nursing groups are selected extremes of continuous maternal behavior, not universal biological classes.

Cross-fostering changes a postnatal care environment. It does not isolate licking from nursing, nutrition or other maternal effects, directly manipulate an abstract neural state, or establish germline inheritance. Same-class foster controls are other mothers, not untouched biological-mother controls.

General adult-age statements conflict with assay-specific 90-day descriptions. ChIP figures report four animals/group but supplementary fixed-tissue methods specify six. GR protein Figure 5a reports five but Western methods specify six. Clones and technical blot replicates are not independent animals; litter dependence remains relevant.

Exon 1_7 is an alternative first exon of the rat glucocorticoid receptor gene. CpG site 16 at the 5-prime end of the NGFI-A binding region and site 17 at its 3-prime end have different outcomes. Bisulfite cytosine readouts, acetyl-H3K9-associated ChIP, NGFI-A ChIP, GR protein and plasma corticosterone are separate observables.

TSA infusion is a broad pharmacological intervention, not a locus-specific methylation edit or cell-specific neural manipulation. The restraint-stress cohort is separate from the GR-protein cohort. Parallel effects do not identify their causal mediation order.

The published Figure 2-associated t/P pairs (2.1/P<0.001 and 3.1/P<0.0001) are inconsistent with ordinary t tests; exact uncertainty is not reproduced. The 27 July 2004 publisher correction fixes labels, corticosterone units to micrograms/dL and bisulfite PCR annealing to 56 degrees C; the supplement retains conflicting text.

Individual animal source values and clone sequences are unavailable in the reviewed materials. Published findings are not an independent reproduction, and nonsignificant contrasts are not equivalence tests.

ODNs were injected 1 h before training; rescue L-lactate (100 nmol) or equicaloric glucose (50 nmol) was injected 15 min before training. Retention was tested at 24 h and 7 days, with 1 h short-term testing in a separate MCT2 assay.

The behavioral endpoint is inhibitory-avoidance entry latency. Supplementary animal, surgical and task procedures and Tables S4-S5 remain unread: age, sex, shock protocol and exact group statistics are not independently established here.

Figure 6 and the MCT2 Results report no lactate rescue; a Discussion sentence inconsistently lists MCT2 among rescued knockdowns. Other Results sentences pair significant impairment with p > 0.05. No numerical inference is derived from those inconsistent passages.

Rescue does not uniquely establish lactate as an exclusive energy substrate; redox, signaling and other metabolic explanations remain possible. The failed equicaloric glucose rescue is dose- and protocol-specific, not proof that glucose can never support retention.

contexts.correctionCheck: Main publication metadata and available indexed records checked. No formal correction resolving the listed source inconsistencies was identified; correction and replication surveillance is incomplete.
contexts.finding: MCT4 and MCT2 knockdowns impaired long-term retention. L-lactate rescued the MCT4 condition; neither lactate nor equicaloric glucose rescued MCT2 knockdown.
limitations: Bilateral hippocampal antisense injections reduce the named transporter in tissue. They are not genetically restricted to a cell class. Astrocytic MCT4 and neuronal MCT2 attribution uses expression evidence; direct cell-to-cell lactate flux was not measured in these behavioral assays.

ODNs were injected 1 h before training; rescue L-lactate (100 nmol) or equicaloric glucose (50 nmol) was injected 15 min before training. Retention was tested at 24 h and 7 days, with 1 h short-term testing in a separate MCT2 assay.

The behavioral endpoint is inhibitory-avoidance entry latency. Supplementary animal, surgical and task procedures and Tables S4-S5 remain unread: age, sex, shock protocol and exact group statistics are not independently established here.

Figure 6 and the MCT2 Results report no lactate rescue; a Discussion sentence inconsistently lists MCT2 among rescued knockdowns. Other Results sentences pair significant impairment with p > 0.05. No numerical inference is derived from those inconsistent passages.

Rescue does not uniquely establish lactate as an exclusive energy substrate; redox, signaling and other metabolic explanations remain possible. The failed equicaloric glucose rescue is dose- and protocol-specific, not proof that glucose can never support retention.

source.title: Dynamic Modulation of Myelination in Response to Visual Stimuli Alters Optic Nerve Conduction Velocity

contexts.correctionCheck: Main publication metadata and available indexed records checked. No formal correction resolving the listed source inconsistencies was identified; correction and replication surveillance is incomplete.
contexts.finding: Deprived preparations had more CC1-positive oligodendrocytes, shorter internodes and slower, broader compound action potentials. Myelin-specific mediation was not isolated.
limitations: Both sexes were used. Long-term eyelid closure starts around P15 and ends at P32. Deprivation changes sensory experience during development; it is not a selective manipulation of myelin, nor elimination of all retinal activity.

CC1 cell counts, NG2-CreERT2/tau-mGFP internodes after P19 tamoxifen, and isolated optic-nerve compound action potentials use distinct assay preparations. They cannot be collapsed into measurements of one axon or a directly identified mediator.
Conduction velocity is nerve length divided by stimulus-to-CAP-peak latency at room temperature. CAP width describes a population waveform, not an identified single-axon speed or information code.

The main text and Figure 3 caption differ on the deprived internode median; Figure 7 repeats Figure 3 group labels, medians and sample counts despite a separate genetic assay. Figure 2 text/caption swap myelinated-axon percentages, and the reported conduction percentage does not directly match the caption means. Exact quantitative calibration remains unadmitted.

Internodes and axons are nested within mice. Raw measurements, animal-clustered uncertainty and plotted values have not been independently reproduced. Ultrastructural and paired-pulse nulls do not prove full equivalence.

contexts.organism: Male and female mice; C57BL/6 and NG2-CreERT2/tau-mGFP assays, deprivation approximately P15-P32
contexts.preparation: Long-term monocular deprivation with separate oligodendrocyte, myelin-internode and isolated optic-nerve conduction assays.

contexts.finding: Deprived preparations had more CC1-positive oligodendrocytes, shorter internodes and slower, broader compound action potentials. Myelin-specific mediation was not isolated.
limitations: Both sexes were used. Long-term eyelid closure starts around P15 and ends at P32. Deprivation changes sensory experience during development; it is not a selective manipulation of myelin, nor elimination of all retinal activity.

CC1 cell counts, NG2-CreERT2/tau-mGFP internodes after P19 tamoxifen, and isolated optic-nerve compound action potentials use distinct assay preparations. They cannot be collapsed into measurements of one axon or a directly identified mediator.
Conduction velocity is nerve length divided by stimulus-to-CAP-peak latency at room temperature. CAP width describes a population waveform, not an identified single-axon speed or information code.

The main text and Figure 3 caption differ on the deprived internode median; Figure 7 repeats Figure 3 group labels, medians and sample counts despite a separate genetic assay. Figure 2 text/caption swap myelinated-axon percentages, and the reported conduction percentage does not directly match the caption means. Exact quantitative calibration remains unadmitted.

Internodes and axons are nested within mice. Raw measurements, animal-clustered uncertainty and plotted values have not been independently reproduced. Ultrastructural and paired-pulse nulls do not prove full equivalence.

contexts.correctionCheck: Publisher/PubMed records and available correction links checked; no notice resolving the stated inconsistencies was identified. This is not exhaustive correction or replication surveillance.
contexts.finding: Selected microglial or purinergic perturbations altered neural readouts, adenosine assays and seizure susceptibility. A1 agonist rescue depended on the genetic preparation.
limitations: Adult seizure cohorts have conflicting descriptions: Animals gives 8-16 weeks for pharmacological experiments, while Seizure Induction gives 14-20 weeks for all seizure experiments. No exact age is selected from this conflict. Genetic cohorts generally include both sexes; pharmacological seizure cohorts are male.

These are distinct genetic preparations. Cx3cr1-CreERT2 targets a lineage rather than proving absolute microglia specificity; P2ry12 deletion is whole-animal, and Drd1a-Cre ligand/receptor deletions are developmental. Cre-negative littermates are the stated default controls.

Neonatal P5-P7 cultures and adult in vivo preparations remain separate. Figure 4c is extracellular striatal dialysate under isoflurane; Figure 4h is a tissue-homogenate fluorescence assay after D1 agonist.

Cortical bouton imaging and striatal calcium imaging are different preparations. The cortical caption says intraperitoneal CNO/clopidogrel while its Methods says intravenous CNO. The neuronal-imaging virus volume and the A1-antagonist dose units also contain unresolved inconsistencies.

Cell and process counts do not replace independent mice. Calcium magnitude and rate-interaction nulls, receptor-specific rescue failures and challenge-specific nulls constrain generalization. Code, raw imaging and all supplementary datasets have not been independently replayed.

Published results and source-table checks are not an independent biological replication. Behavioral stage IV-V seizures are an induced challenge endpoint, not a universal measure of neural stability or a human treatment result.

contexts.correctionCheck: Publisher/PubMed records and available correction links checked; no notice resolving the stated inconsistencies was identified. This is not exhaustive correction or replication surveillance.
contexts.finding: Selected microglial or purinergic perturbations altered neural readouts, adenosine assays and seizure susceptibility. A1 agonist rescue depended on the genetic preparation.
limitations: Adult seizure cohorts have conflicting descriptions: Animals gives 8-16 weeks for pharmacological experiments, while Seizure Induction gives 14-20 weeks for all seizure experiments. No exact age is selected from this conflict. Genetic cohorts generally include both sexes; pharmacological seizure cohorts are male.

These are distinct genetic preparations. Cx3cr1-CreERT2 targets a lineage rather than proving absolute microglia specificity; P2ry12 deletion is whole-animal, and Drd1a-Cre ligand/receptor deletions are developmental. Cre-negative littermates are the stated default controls.

Neonatal P5-P7 cultures and adult in vivo preparations remain separate. Figure 4c is extracellular striatal dialysate under isoflurane; Figure 4h is a tissue-homogenate fluorescence assay after D1 agonist.

Cortical bouton imaging and striatal calcium imaging are different preparations. The cortical caption says intraperitoneal CNO/clopidogrel while its Methods says intravenous CNO. The neuronal-imaging virus volume and the A1-antagonist dose units also contain unresolved inconsistencies.

Cell and process counts do not replace independent mice. Calcium magnitude and rate-interaction nulls, receptor-specific rescue failures and challenge-specific nulls constrain generalization. Code, raw imaging and all supplementary datasets have not been independently replayed.

Published results and source-table checks are not an independent biological replication. Behavioral stage IV-V seizures are an induced challenge endpoint, not a universal measure of neural stability or a human treatment result.

contexts.correctionCheck: Main publication metadata and available indexed records checked. No formal correction resolving the listed source inconsistencies was identified; correction and replication surveillance is incomplete.
contexts.finding: Relative activity perturbations changed engulfment preference. CR3/C3 loss reduced engulfment; CR3 loss increased projection overlap and structural synaptic puncta.
limitations: The preparation is the developing mouse retinogeniculate system. Engulfment is assayed at P5, segregation at P10/P30 and synaptic puncta at P32-35. Adult maintenance, immune surveillance, disease and all brain regions are not established by these developmental endpoints.

TTX/forskolin are intraocular pharmacological manipulations; CTB labeling follows 4-5 h later. Left-eye drug and right-eye vehicle inputs are compared within selected dLGN regions. Relative labeled-input engulfment is not a direct measurement of every synapse firing rate.

CR3/CD11b and C3 knockouts are developmental whole-animal genotypes. Local attribution to microglia is supported by CR3 expression and absence of other CR3-positive cells in the inspected P5 dLGN; the manipulation is not a microglia-restricted inducible knockout.

CTB-positive volume inside reconstructed microglia, projection overlap and juxtaposed VGlut2/GluR1 puncta are distinct anatomical observables. They do not directly measure synaptic efficacy or prove one exclusive sequence of activity, complement tagging and engulfment.

Engulfment is reduced, not abolished, in CR3/C3 knockouts. Complement-independent and nonphagocytic mechanisms remain possible. Raw images, complete supplementary methods and the updated supplementary document remain unread; sex is not established by the selected main methods.

contexts.correctionCheck: PMC and publisher metadata and exact-DOI notice searches checked on 13 September 2026; no resolving correction identified. This is not exhaustive notice surveillance. Online publication 29 November 2009; issue date 17 December 2009.
contexts.finding: Novel motor training is accompanied by increased formation and elimination in selected cortical dendrites, and initially new spines are preferentially retained. The results constrain experience-dependent remodeling without proving a unique memory substrate or a universal construction law.
limitations: YFP-H mice were one month old or older than four months. Superficial apical dendrites of layer V pyramidal neurons were imaged 10-100 micrometers below the cortical surface under ketamine-xylazine anesthesia; these are selected cortical compartments, not a whole-brain connectome.

Main scientific text, Methods Summary and Figures 1-4 are reviewed. All text of the 12-page publisher supplement, Figures S1-S5 and Table S1 are reviewed, including visual inspection. The separate full Methods file and movie were not obtained or read; precise task procedures, sex, allocation, blinding and exclusions remain unverified.

Dense labeling prevented tracing complete individual neurons. The supplementary estimate of 20-80 sampled cells per mouse is not an identified neuron census. The study total of 32079 spines in 209 mice does not make spines independent animals or mean that every spine was followed for 120 days.

Formation and elimination are interval-specific percentages relative to the initial spine count. New-spine survival uses the newly appearing subset instead. These denominators cannot be exchanged or converted into universal growth rates, absolute density or graph weights.

General controls were littermates with the same food restriction and similar handling, without shaping or training. Learning, task exposure and reward are not individually isolated. Animal-level image stacks, cohort assignments and analysis code were not obtained; published tests were not independently reproduced.

The Figure 1f first-session training group selected four mice with more than ten successes in thirty reaches. Figure 1g also plots animals with ten or fewer successes, so the correlation cohort is not this selected four-mouse group. Imaging occurred within one hour after the session, but the baseline was from the previous day; this interval does not timestamp each spine birth within an hour.

Behavioral curves, spine-turnover cohorts and follow-up cohorts have different animal counts. The survival design uses two classification images and a third follow-up at a selected interval; it is not one fully sampled trajectory through every plotted timepoint.

Figure 2c normalizes total spine number to the initial image. Both control and trained trajectories lie below their initial value by day 16. Convergence toward control levels is distinct from the abstract wording about return to the original level; no exact count setpoint or one-for-one replacement is demonstrated.

Spine morphology does not directly measure synaptic currents, presynaptic partner identity or memory content. The study does not selectively remove the retained spines to test memory necessity or uniquely assign different memories to disjoint synaptic sets.

Motor mapping was terminal in fourteen mice: five imaging regions lay within the forelimb map, six on its border and three outside but within 300 micrometers. The map was not followed longitudinally, and distance from its border does not identify a complete circuit or a construction geometry.

Named nonsignificant comparisons are not equivalence tests. The long-duration activity controls had marked attrition: only two mice still reached more than twenty times daily at day eight and one at day sixteen. They do not support a well-powered universal exclusion of motor activity.

Spine-size analysis used head diameter divided by adjacent shaft diameter in 29 surviving spines; the cited supplementary paragraph does not supply its animal count. This selected morphological ratio is neither absolute spine volume nor measured synaptic strength.

Persistence to the reported approximately 120-day follow-up is finite. Training for sixteen days followed by the long untrained interval does not demonstrate permanence, a globally minimal circuit or a unique homeostatic construction law.

contexts.finding: Novel motor training is accompanied by increased formation and elimination in selected cortical dendrites, and initially new spines are preferentially retained. The results constrain experience-dependent remodeling without proving a unique memory substrate or a universal construction law.
limitations: YFP-H mice were one month old or older than four months. Superficial apical dendrites of layer V pyramidal neurons were imaged 10-100 micrometers below the cortical surface under ketamine-xylazine anesthesia; these are selected cortical compartments, not a whole-brain connectome.

Main scientific text, Methods Summary and Figures 1-4 are reviewed. All text of the 12-page publisher supplement, Figures S1-S5 and Table S1 are reviewed, including visual inspection.
