contexts.finding: Selected peri-infarct samples show increased spine formation and altered morphology after photothrombosis. Recovery cohorts, optical readouts and spatial comparisons constrain injury-associated remodeling without proving behavioral restoration or a unique construction mechanism.
limitations: Adult male C57BL6 YFP-H mice were approximately 2.5-7 months old. Layer 5 neuronal apical tufts were sampled within the superficial 100 micrometers, typically 100-500 micrometers from the posterior-medial infarct edge; this is selected surviving cortex, not the whole injured brain.

Main scientific text, Materials and Methods, and Figures 1-5 with captions are reviewed. Supplemental Figures 1-2 were not obtained or read. Animal-identified image stacks, custom IgorPro routines and the allocation/exclusion manifest were not obtained; no imaging or biological experiment was independently reproduced.

Photothrombosis used Rose Bengal 100 milligrams per kilogram intraperitoneally and 532-nanometer illumination, 17 milliwatts for fifteen minutes, under ketamine-xylazine. Sham controls omitted either dye or illumination. Per-assay sham composition, random allocation and group-specific age distributions are not supplied in the reviewed account.

Imaging under urethane was acute: hourly stacks over six, occasionally seven hours, after a one-, two- or six-week recovery interval, followed by terminal histology. Separate cohorts do not trace the same spine or dendritic arbor continuously from before injury through six weeks.

Only laterally projecting spines were scored. New spines had to protrude at least four pixels, approximately 0.55 micrometers, and remain present at the six-hour endpoint. Transient events, filopodium conversions, shifted segments and poor-quality images were excluded. The assay is not a census of all spine births, losses or synapses.

Turnover is reported as a percentage of the counted spine population over the imaging session; raw animal-level numerator/denominator assignments are unavailable. Spine density is a count per ten micrometers of dendrite. Neither measure is a neuron birth rate, a universal hourly turnover constant or a calibrated graph weight.

Turnover scoring was blinded to experimental condition, but movement, abnormal breathing and image deterioration could exclude experiments; exclusion counts and animal identifiers are not supplied. Axial optical resolution was about 5.3 micrometers, much poorer than lateral resolution, and six spine-appearance cases were pooled across animals for shaft-fluorescence controls.

Spine morphology and adjacent sensory-evoked reflectance do not measure the functional efficacy of each new synapse, selective memory content or behavioral recovery. The Discussion explicitly leaves the causal link between increased formation and recovered function unestablished.

The main text gives a 0.14 percent control formation mean and 1.37, 0.93 and 0.75 percent poststroke means. The abstract describes a five- to eight-fold peak increase; these rounded quantities do not define one exact fold estimate. Retain the reported assay means without calibrating a universal multiplier.

The six-week density cohort reports five mice versus six controls but t(8)=1.43, P=0.09. The three-mouse near/far comparison reports t(3)=4.87, P<0.01 for formation and t(3)=1.92, P=0.08 for elimination. Sidedness and statistical units need resolution before numerical reproduction; these degrees of freedom do not establish an ordinary paired three-mouse test.

Orientation uses projected 15-30 micrometer segments, eighteen ten-degree bins, and three mice per group, with the infarct placed at a common reference position. Reported F(17,17) tests concern bin-distribution variance; bins are not independent mice and this is not an animal-level circular-statistical reconstruction.

The authors consider mechanical distortion during tissue loss and scar formation as well as growth and retraction. Projected dendrite-vessel alignment does not isolate shared guidance, establish physical contact or prove an optimal generative network geometry.

Texas Red dextran labels plasma. Capillary velocity in micrometers per second is distinct from volumetric perfusion; fluorescent vessel volume fraction is distinct from vessel number, connectivity and selectively demonstrated angiogenesis. The vascular cohort totals fourteen animals but per-timepoint assignments and segmentation routines remain unresolved.

The near/far spine comparison uses approximately 0.33 versus 1.65 millimeters from the infarct edge at two weeks. This is different from the orientation comparison of less than 250 versus 500-800 micrometers at six weeks. Restricted ipsilateral sampling does not establish absence of remodeling elsewhere.

Nonsignificant outcomes are not equivalence or full recovery. Photothrombosis does not permit controlled reperfusion, and the paper does not directly establish the same time course in other stroke models, traumatic injury or humans.

Axial optical resolution was about 5.3 micrometers, much poorer than lateral resolution, and six spine-appearance cases were pooled across animals for shaft-fluorescence controls.

contexts.finding: Selected peri-infarct samples show increased spine formation and altered morphology after photothrombosis. Recovery cohorts, optical readouts and spatial comparisons constrain injury-associated remodeling without proving behavioral restoration or a unique construction mechanism.
limitations: Adult male C57BL6 YFP-H mice were approximately 2.5-7 months old. Layer 5 neuronal apical tufts were sampled within the superficial 100 micrometers, typically 100-500 micrometers from the posterior-medial infarct edge; this is selected surviving cortex, not the whole injured brain.

Sham controls omitted either dye or illumination. Per-assay sham composition, random allocation and group-specific age distributions are not supplied in the reviewed account.

Imaging under urethane was acute: hourly stacks over six, occasionally seven hours, after a one-, two- or six-week recovery interval, followed by terminal histology. Separate cohorts do not trace the same spine or dendritic arbor continuously from before injury through six weeks.

Only laterally projecting spines were scored. New spines had to protrude at least four pixels, approximately 0.55 micrometers, and remain present at the six-hour endpoint. Transient events, filopodium conversions, shifted segments and poor-quality images were excluded. The assay is not a census of all spine births, losses or synapses.

Spine density is a count per ten micrometers of dendrite. Neither measure is a neuron birth rate, a universal hourly turnover constant or a calibrated graph weight.

Turnover scoring was blinded to experimental condition, but movement, abnormal breathing and image deterioration could exclude experiments; exclusion counts and animal identifiers are not supplied. Axial optical resolution was about 5.3 micrometers, much poorer than lateral resolution, and six spine-appearance cases were pooled across animals for shaft-fluorescence controls.

Spine morphology and adjacent sensory-evoked reflectance do not measure the functional efficacy of each new synapse, selective memory content or behavioral recovery. The Discussion explicitly leaves the causal link between increased formation and recovered function unestablished.

The main text gives a 0.14 percent control formation mean and 1.37, 0.93 and 0.75 percent poststroke means. The abstract describes a five- to eight-fold peak increase; these rounded quantities do not define one exact fold estimate. Retain the reported assay means without calibrating a universal multiplier.

The six-week density cohort reports five mice versus six controls but t(8)=1.43, P=0.09. The three-mouse near/far comparison reports t(3)=4.87, P<0.01 for formation and t(3)=1.92, P=0.08 for elimination. Sidedness and statistical units need resolution before numerical reproduction; these degrees of freedom do not establish an ordinary paired three-mouse test.

Orientation uses projected 15-30 micrometer segments, eighteen ten-degree bins, and three mice per group, with the infarct placed at a common reference position. Reported F(17,17) tests concern bin-distribution variance; bins are not independent mice and this is not an animal-level circular-statistical reconstruction.

The authors consider mechanical distortion during tissue loss and scar formation as well as growth and retraction. Projected dendrite-vessel alignment does not isolate shared guidance, establish physical contact or prove an optimal generative network geometry.

Texas Red dextran labels plasma. Capillary velocity in micrometers per second is distinct from volumetric perfusion; fluorescent vessel volume fraction is distinct from vessel number, connectivity and selectively demonstrated angiogenesis. The vascular cohort totals fourteen animals but per-timepoint assignments and segmentation routines remain unresolved.

The near/far spine comparison uses approximately 0.33 versus 1.65 millimeters from the infarct edge at two weeks. This is different from the orientation comparison of less than 250 versus 500-800 micrometers at six weeks. Restricted ipsilateral sampling does not establish absence of remodeling elsewhere.

Nonsignificant outcomes are not equivalence or full recovery. Photothrombosis does not permit controlled reperfusion, and the paper does not directly establish the same time course in other stroke models, traumatic injury or humans.

Main scientific text, Materials and Methods, and Figures 1-5 with captions are reviewed. Supplemental Figures 1-2 were not obtained or read. Animal-identified image stacks, custom IgorPro routines and the allocation/exclusion manifest were not obtained; no imaging or biological experiment was independently reproduced.

Photothrombosis used Rose Bengal 100 milligrams per kilogram intraperitoneally and 532-nanometer illumination, 17 milliwatts for fifteen minutes, under ketamine-xylazine. Sham controls omitted either dye or illumination. Per-assay sham composition, random allocation and group-specific age distributions are not supplied in the reviewed account.

Imaging under urethane was acute: hourly stacks over six, occasionally seven hours, after a one-, two- or six-week recovery interval, followed by terminal histology. Separate cohorts do not trace the same spine or dendritic arbor continuously from before injury through six weeks.

Only laterally projecting spines were scored. New spines had to protrude at least four pixels, approximately 0.55 micrometers, and remain present at the six-hour endpoint. Transient events, filopodium conversions, shifted segments and poor-quality images were excluded. The assay is not a census of all spine births, losses or synapses.

Turnover is reported as a percentage of the counted spine population over the imaging session; raw animal-level numerator/denominator assignments are unavailable. Spine density is a count per ten micrometers of dendrite. Neither measure is a neuron birth rate, a universal hourly turnover constant or a calibrated graph weight.

Turnover scoring was blinded to experimental condition, but movement, abnormal breathing and image deterioration could exclude experiments; exclusion counts and animal identifiers are not supplied. Axial optical resolution was about 5.3 micrometers, much poorer than lateral resolution, and six spine-appearance cases were pooled across animals for shaft-fluorescence controls.

Spine morphology and adjacent sensory-evoked reflectance do not measure the functional efficacy of each new synapse, selective memory content or behavioral recovery. The Discussion explicitly leaves the causal link between increased formation and recovered function unestablished.

The main text gives a 0.14 percent control formation mean and 1.37, 0.93 and 0.75 percent poststroke means. The abstract describes a five- to eight-fold peak increase; these rounded quantities do not define one exact fold estimate. Retain the reported assay means without calibrating a universal multiplier.

The six-week density cohort reports five mice versus six controls but t(8)=1.43, P=0.09. The three-mouse near/far comparison reports t(3)=4.87, P<0.01 for formation and t(3)=1.92, P=0.08 for elimination. Sidedness and statistical units need resolution before numerical reproduction; these degrees of freedom do not establish an ordinary paired three-mouse test.

Orientation uses projected 15-30 micrometer segments, eighteen ten-degree bins, and three mice per group, with the infarct placed at a common reference position. Reported F(17,17) tests concern bin-distribution variance; bins are not independent mice and this is not an animal-level circular-statistical reconstruction.

The authors consider mechanical distortion during tissue loss and scar formation as well as growth and retraction. Projected dendrite-vessel alignment does not isolate shared guidance, establish physical contact or prove an optimal generative network geometry.

Texas Red dextran labels plasma. Capillary velocity in micrometers per second is distinct from volumetric perfusion; fluorescent vessel volume fraction is distinct from vessel number, connectivity and selectively demonstrated angiogenesis. The vascular cohort totals fourteen animals but per-timepoint assignments and segmentation routines remain unresolved.

The near/far spine comparison uses approximately 0.33 versus 1.65 millimeters from the infarct edge at two weeks. This is different from the orientation comparison of less than 250 versus 500-800 micrometers at six weeks. Restricted ipsilateral sampling does not establish absence of remodeling elsewhere.

Nonsignificant outcomes are not equivalence or full recovery. Photothrombosis does not permit controlled reperfusion, and the paper does not directly establish the same time course in other stroke models, traumatic injury or humans.

contexts.correctionCheck: Publisher and PubMed metadata and exact-DOI correction searches checked. DOI 10.1038/nn.4542 is a commentary, not an erratum. No identified correction resolves the listed reporting conflicts; this is not exhaustive notice surveillance.
contexts.finding: Capillary potassium evokes upstream dilation and hyperpolarization and increased RBC passage under specified conditions. Endothelial Kcnj2 deletion reduces the whisker perfusion response without eliminating it.
limitations: Adult male mice; Online Methods state two to three months, but Supplementary Table 2 reports mean ages of 14.8 weeks for C57BL/6 and 17.0 weeks for knockout laser-Doppler cohorts. No exact universal age range is admitted. No randomization, blinding, prospective sample-size calculation or exclusions were reported.

Kcnj2 deletion uses constitutive Tek-Cre, not adult-induced capillary-only deletion. Isolated cEC currents and control smooth-muscle currents support endothelial attribution but do not exclude developmental effects or establish restriction to one vascular segment. Identical listed genotyping primer pairs require verification before protocol reproduction.

Whole-cell currents are measured with 60 mM external potassium; this recording solution is distinct from 10 mM focal capillary stimulation, 15 mM cortical superfusion and physiological neural release. Kir2.1/Kcnj2 is the primary molecular identity. Ba2+ also blocks vascular Kir channels outside capillary endothelium.

CaPA is an isolated, pressurized preparation with sealed capillary ends, not normal flowing blood. Diameter, upstream smooth-muscle voltage and in vivo flux come from separate recordings. Membrane-potential recordings use wortmannin to suppress movement. Estimated conduction speed is inferred from distance and onset, not voltage measured along every endothelial cell.

In vivo measurements use acute cranial windows and alpha-chloralose/urethane after isoflurane surgery. RBC flux is cells per second; velocity is distance per time; laser Doppler gives a relative tissue perfusion signal. None is BOLD, oxygen consumption or an exact anatomical network reconstruction.

Peak RBC flux is the maximum one-second bin in an approximately seventeen-second post-stimulus interval relative to about three seconds of baseline. Velocity is sampled in the peak-flux bin, not an independently selected peak. Paired observations and nested capillaries are not independent mice.

The Figure 4 diameter null concerns eighteen capillaries in seven mice; the authors state that sampled measurement sites lacked pericytes. Upstream diameter uses eight paired experiments in seven mice. The local null does not exclude pericyte effects at other segments or prove equivalence.

Whisker responses persist after endothelial Kcnj2 deletion. Surface barium has a broader target range and leaves residual perfusion responses. The potassium source during neural activity and the complete intercellular route remain unresolved; potassium ejection bypasses the physiological release step.

Supplementary Figure 5 reports five preparations but paired t statistics with five degrees of freedom; Figure 7 reports group sizes inconsistent with its unpaired-test degrees of freedom. Supplementary Table 1 and Table 2 also reverse control-line sample counts for the flow comparisons. Exact quantitative calibration requires animal-identified measurements and resolution.

Nonsignificance is not equivalence. The selected SK/IK activation protocols do not exclude every calcium-dependent endothelial channel. The LFP control tests selected spectral bands, not complete neural activity, and the TTX potassium experiment does not identify the physiological potassium-releasing cell.

Raw recordings and custom MATLAB LFP software have not been obtained or reproduced. The reporting checklist and main text do not provide a resolved access route. No numerical edge weights, universal minimal carrier counts or independently validated full pathway are assigned.

contexts.correctionCheck: Publisher/PMC metadata and exact-DOI correction searches checked on 13 September 2026; no resolving notice was identified. This is not exhaustive notice surveillance. Published online 11 July 2008; August 2008 issue.
contexts.finding: Labeled granule-cell populations produce functional output in selected slices. Direct versus indirect routes and cross-sectional morphology constrain circuit hypotheses without establishing behavior or a unique construction sequence.
limitations: Female C57BL/6 mice received retrovirus at five to seven weeks in Methods, versus six to seven weeks in Results, after three to seven days of running-wheel access. Anatomy at 17, 28 and 75 days after labeling and later slice physiology are separate samples, not uniform mature-adult stages.

Functional recording covered 43 slices from 34 mice at 8.6-20.6 weeks after labeling. Fourteen responding target cells came from 11 slices of nine mice at 13.4-20.4 weeks. Most recordings used 200 micromolar BaCl2 to increase excitability and all-trans retinal to assist ChR2; these are not ordinary in vivo signaling conditions.

Broad illumination activates a labeled population, not a single presynaptic neuron. CAG-ChR2-GFP and PGK-ChR2-IRES-RFP are different constructs. ChR2 expression changes with age and affects spike latency and capture; normal-looking morphology is not an equivalence test for absence of opsin effects.

Of 107 sampled targets, 76 were classified as interneurons, 16 as mossy cells, 11 as pyramidal cells and four remained unclassified. Fourteen responded: 11 interneurons, one mossy cell, one CA3 pyramidal cell and one unclassified cell. This selected yield is not a connection probability. Supplementary Table 1 classification samples have different denominators.

Kynurenic acid blocks upstream glutamatergic transmission in direct and indirect routes. Bicuculline sensitivity in two of five tested targets supports a polysynaptic inhibitory component, including the illustrated CA3 pyramidal response; it does not establish direct newborn-neuron excitation of that pyramidal cell.

Seven of 14 responses were judged probably monosynaptic from kinetics, latency and pharmacology; two were probably polysynaptic and five were not resolved. Latency is measured from light onset, includes opsin-dependent presynaptic spiking and is not a directly measured synaptic delay or unique hop count.

Bouton selection requires size above three axon diameters, connection to an axon and isolation for tracing. Cross-sectional confocal and electron-microscopic samples do not trace bouton replacement over time or provide an unbiased population geometry. Mouse allocation and the mapping between contact-census and profile-analysis denominators are incomplete.

CA3 contact censuses at 17, 28 and 75 days use eight, eleven and twelve boutons; the largest-section analyses use seven, nine and ten. Di-aminobenzidine labeling can obscure vesicles. The active-zone omnibus P=0.12 coexists with a significant reported post hoc contrast; this does not support uniform growth across all measures.

Main captions label some ANOVA statistics as t; the main Methods specify Fisher PLSD after significant ANOVA whereas Supplementary Table 1 uses Tukey comparisons. One brain was excluded for insufficient labeling. Complete animal allocation, blinding, sample-size planning and raw-recording manifests are unavailable.

Main experimental text, Methods, Figures 1-5 and the complete four-page supplement were read; all main and supplementary figures and Table 1 were visually inspected. Raw recordings, animal-identified measurements and analysis code were not obtained or replayed.

The study measures morphology and output transmission, not behavior. Proposed recruitment of existing spines is a cross-sectional interpretation, not an observed minimal construction rule or proof of memory necessity.

Photometry uses saline on day 4 and LPS on day 5 in the same animals. Vagotomized mice form a separate group after two weeks of recovery; a matched abdominal sham is not explicitly specified in the reviewed procedure. Figure 1c reports residual responses after an approximately 80% reduction.

LPS doses differ across assays: 50 micrograms/kg for FOS and TRAP, 0.5 mg/kg for the main photometry comparison, 0.1 mg/kg for cytokine chemogenetics and 12.5 mg/kg for survival. These exposures are not interchangeable. LPS endotoxaemia is distinct from viable bacterial infection.

Extended Data 8e shows two IL-10/fat co-responders among 63 neurons, which the authors did not consider further. Universal zero overlap is unsupported.

Injected cytokines and extraintestinal perfusion have different doses, routes and recording windows. The response classifier uses baseline median absolute deviation, a mean modified z-score above 1.6 and peak fluorescence of at least 1%. Selected, normalized responder heatmaps are not an unbiased full-population distribution. In vivo responses do not establish direct cytokine binding to a neuronal receptor; epithelial or immune intermediates remain possible. Referenced imaging procedures have not been fully audited.

Lower circulating inflammatory cytokines do not imply universally better defense: sustained TRPA1-population activation increased Salmonella tissue burden in the separate live-infection assay.

Raw measurements, animal identifiers and custom code have not been obtained or replayed. Exclusion criteria include unsuccessful targeting/expression/ablation, but counts and operational thresholds are incomplete. Extended Data 9c reports Gpr65 IL-6 P=0.03 despite a broad no-appreciable-effect conclusion; its small plotted decrease must not be turned into an all-population null. No numerical edge weight or universal carrier count is assigned.

The DSS Methods specify CNO in the experimental cohort drinking solution, while Figure 6 says all animals received CNO. Matched control exposure and intake need resolution before a selective DSS mechanism is admitted. This issue does not change the separately described injected-CNO LPS or infection protocols.

contexts.finding: Relative activity perturbations changed engulfment preference. CR3/C3 loss reduced engulfment; CR3 loss increased projection overlap and structural synaptic puncta.
limitations: The preparation is the developing mouse retinogeniculate system. Engulfment is assayed at P5, segregation at P10/P30 and synaptic puncta at P32-35. Adult maintenance, immune surveillance, disease and all brain regions are not established by these developmental endpoints.

TTX/forskolin are intraocular pharmacological manipulations; CTB labeling follows 4-5 h later. Left-eye drug and right-eye vehicle inputs are compared within selected dLGN regions. Relative labeled-input engulfment is not a direct measurement of every synapse firing rate.

CR3/CD11b and C3 knockouts are developmental whole-animal genotypes. Local attribution to microglia is supported by CR3 expression and absence of other CR3-positive cells in the inspected P5 dLGN; the manipulation is not a microglia-restricted inducible knockout.

CTB-positive volume inside reconstructed microglia, projection overlap and juxtaposed VGlut2/GluR1 puncta are distinct anatomical observables. They do not directly measure synaptic efficacy or prove one exclusive sequence of activity, complement tagging and engulfment.

Engulfment is reduced, not abolished, in CR3/C3 knockouts. Complement-independent and nonphagocytic mechanisms remain possible. Raw images, complete supplementary methods and the updated supplementary document remain unread; sex is not established by the selected main methods.

contexts.correctionCheck: Publisher and PubMed records and exact-title notice searches checked. No identified notice resolves the specified method, control or label issues; this is not exhaustive correction or replication surveillance.
contexts.finding: Peripheral challenges evoked neural readouts, while selected neural manipulations changed circulating cytokines. Activation improved high-dose endotoxin survival but increased bacterial tissue load in a different live-infection protocol. A complete descending immune circuit is not identified.
limitations: Both male and female mice at least seven weeks old were used; exact age and sex distributions per assay group are not supplied. No randomized animal allocation, blinded investigation or prospective statistical sample-size calculation is reported. The reporting summary discusses stimulus ordering separately; it does not establish randomized animal groups.

FOS labeling is an activity-associated marker; Vglut2-cre bulk GCaMP6s is a population calcium signal, not a DBH-specific spike recording. Photometry uses saline on day 4 and LPS on day 5 in the same animals. Vagotomized mice form a separate group after two weeks of recovery; a matched abdominal sham is not explicitly specified in the reviewed procedure. Figure 1c reports residual responses after an approximately 80% reduction.

LPS doses differ across assays: 50 micrograms/kg for FOS and TRAP, 0.5 mg/kg for the main photometry comparison, 0.1 mg/kg for cytokine chemogenetics and 12.5 mg/kg for survival. These exposures are not interchangeable. LPS endotoxaemia is distinct from viable bacterial infection.

Fos-based TRAP2 labeling is followed by at least four weeks before functional rechallenge to restore LPS sensitivity. LPS-TRAPed, Dbh-cre, Vglut2-cre and Vgat-cre populations are not identical. Dbh expression does not measure norepinephrine release or identify a unique molecular mediator.

For standard cytokine chemogenetics, Methods specify CNO at 2 mg/kg twelve hours and 1 mg/kg one hour before challenge; schematics and captions show only the one-hour pretreatment. mCherry controls receive CNO. Saline/LPS tests use the same cohort at least seven days apart, whereas hM3Dq/hM4Di versus mCherry comparisons use separate groups. Blood ELISA at two hours does not identify cytokine-producing cells.

Cre-defined nodose activation perturbs marker-defined neurons; it is not selective activation of the TRPA1 channel or CALCA peptide. TRPA1 neurons include different stimulus-responsive subgroups. Extended Data 8e shows two IL-10/fat co-responders among 63 neurons, which the authors did not consider further. Universal zero overlap is unsupported.

Injected cytokines and extraintestinal perfusion have different doses, routes and recording windows. The response classifier uses baseline median absolute deviation, a mean modified z-score above 1.6 and peak fluorescence of at least 1%. Selected, normalized responder heatmaps are not an unbiased full-population distribution. In vivo responses do not establish direct cytokine binding to a neuronal receptor; epithelial or immune intermediates remain possible. Referenced imaging procedures have not been fully audited.

Survival experiments use separate Trpa1-cre nodose and Dbh-cre cNST cohorts after high-dose LPS, with repeated 5 mg/kg CNO dosing. Figure 6 shows survival through nine days, not a lifelong or clinical outcome. Separate infection experiments use oral Salmonella and eight CNO injections beginning twelve hours before inoculation; bacterial load is measured in spleen and mesenteric lymph nodes at day five.

Nonsignificance is not equivalence or proof of no pathway contribution. The corticosterone null is a two-hour circulating concentration, not complete exclusion of hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal mediation. Extended Data 3 reuses the Figure 2c saline/LPS data; it is not an independent replication.

The cNST transcriptomic atlas pools tissue from five animals; 4,008 cells and expression clusters are not independent animal replicates, anatomical coordinates or a measured connectome. Rabies labeling supports an anatomical input interpretation, not synaptic efficacy. Main text calls the rabies reporter dsRed while Methods and Extended Data 12 specify GFP; panel 12d depicts Trpa1 but repeats Calca in its quantitative caption. No tracing fraction is calibrated.

Descending efferent routes and immune effector cells remain unresolved. A whole-animal Myd88 knockout does not isolate immune-cell-specific mediation. Lower circulating inflammatory cytokines do not imply universally better defense: sustained TRPA1-population activation increased Salmonella tissue burden in the separate live-infection assay.

Raw measurements, animal identifiers and custom code have not been obtained or replayed. Exclusion criteria include unsuccessful targeting/expression/ablation, but counts and operational thresholds are incomplete. Extended Data 9c reports Gpr65 IL-6 P=0.03 despite a broad no-appreciable-effect conclusion; its small plotted decrease must not be turned into an all-population null. No numerical edge weight or universal carrier count is assigned.

The DSS Methods specify CNO in the experimental cohort drinking solution, while Figure 6 says all animals received CNO. Matched control exposure and intake need resolution before a selective DSS mechanism is admitted. This issue does not change the separately described injected-CNO LPS or infection protocols.

Extended Data 9c reports Gpr65 IL-6 P=0.03 despite a broad no-appreciable-effect conclusion; its small plotted decrease must not be turned into an all-population null. No numerical edge weight or universal carrier count is assigned.

contexts.finding: The reported picture-category contrasts depend on region, frequency, summary and preprocessing.
limitations: Twenty-nine patients were recruited; one accuracy and six electrode-location exclusions leave twenty-two. Electrode placement follows clinical need. The four selected regions do not define a complete or minimal empathy circuit.

The 0-500 ms analysis excludes the later response period, but does not isolate all attention, motor preparation or salience effects. Nonsignificant accuracy and reaction-time contrasts are not equivalence tests.

Channels and pairs are nested in patients and can share references. For ACC-amygdala, 72 pairs come from only four patients. Mixed-model sensitivity analyses use already selected regions and windows from the same observations.

The default clean-white-matter average reference, wavelet resolution, baseline normalization, smoothing and cluster criteria constrain timing and coupling. Nearest-reference and 50 ms smoothing results do not retain every original effect at the original threshold.
No neural intervention, actual self-pain, helping outcome, healthy-control iEEG or individual working-memory dependency is tested. Raw EEG and the full processing pipeline have not been reproduced.

limitations: Twenty-nine patients were recruited; one accuracy and six electrode-location exclusions leave twenty-two. Electrode placement follows clinical need. The four selected regions do not define a complete or minimal empathy circuit.

The 0-500 ms analysis excludes the later response period, but does not isolate all attention, motor preparation or salience effects. Nonsignificant accuracy and reaction-time contrasts are not equivalence tests.

Channels and pairs are nested in patients and can share references. For ACC-amygdala, 72 pairs come from only four patients. Mixed-model sensitivity analyses use already selected regions and windows from the same observations.

The default clean-white-matter average reference, wavelet resolution, baseline normalization, smoothing and cluster criteria constrain timing and coupling. Nearest-reference and 50 ms smoothing results do not retain every original effect at the original threshold.
No neural intervention, actual self-pain, helping outcome, healthy-control iEEG or individual working-memory dependency is tested. Raw EEG and the full processing pipeline have not been reproduced.

contexts.correctionCheck: Publisher metadata, the author-lab PDF and publisher supplementary PDF, and exact DOI correction, erratum and retraction searches were checked on 14 September 2026. No notice resolving the stated dose, reporter or denominator conflicts was identified. This is not exhaustive correction surveillance.
contexts.finding: PV activation suppresses population cycle markers and PV inhibition increases them; tested SST/VIP manipulations retain nulls. Conditional gamma2 deletion changes early activation and later clone composition. Isolation retains an EdU difference under PV activation, while MCM2 housing contrasts are nonsignificant. Full feedback closure and exclusive mediation remain unresolved.
limitations: Adult mouse preparations use nestin-GFP, PV/SST/VIP-Cre and nestin-CreERT2;Z/EG lines with gamma2-floxed or control alleles. Sex and a complete group-specific animal manifest are not reported. Tamoxifen is a single 62 mg/kg intraperitoneal dose at 6-10 weeks. The Methods require at least four weeks after AAV surgery; schematic week labels do not supply exact ages for every animal.

Acute 300-micrometre slices were recorded at 32-34 degrees C, with RGL voltage clamp at -65 mV and 5 mM kynurenic acid. The internal solution is ambiguously printed as 135 mM CsCl gluconate. Clamp-current sign does not directly identify native membrane polarization, spiking or cell-cycle entry.

Main text, Online Methods and Supplementary Figure 1 print 200 mM for focal GABA/muscimol application; no micromolar substitution is made. Etomidate is 100 nM in the main text/Figure 1 but 10 micromolar in Methods. The etomidate dose remains unresolved, and pharmacological sensitivity does not establish receptor stoichiometry.

Population experiments use five consecutive days of stimulation, eight hours per day: ChR2 blue light at 472 nm, 5-ms pulses at 8 Hz for 30 seconds every five minutes, or continuous 593-nm eNpHR light. AAV volume, delivered light power and a full opsin-negative illumination control are not reported. No-light sham comparisons include the effects of the complete light protocol.

On day five, EdU is injected intraperitoneally at 41.1 mg/kg six times, two hours apart, with collection two hours after the last injection. Repeated injections are not independent replicates. EdU incorporation and MCM2 expression are cycle-related endpoints, not counts of completed neuronal differentiation, integrated neurons or an instantaneous birth rate.

Population scoring uses 40-micrometre sections, every sixth section, and nestin-positive inverted-Y morphology over an EdU- or MCM2-positive nucleus. Optogenetic counts are limited to one millimetre anterior and posterior to the injection. Densities per cubic millimetre and the MCM2-positive fraction have distinct denominators. Analyses are described as blinded; random assignment, raw unit records and multiplicity-adjusted tests are not supplied.

At two and seven days after induction, one GFP-positive RGL is classified as a quiescent clone and two or more nuclei as an activated clone. These are fixed-tissue, spatially assigned clones using a referenced method, not live observations of every division or independently verified common ancestry. Supplementary Figure 2d plots one dentate gyrus per dot; hemispheres and clones cannot automatically be treated as independent animals.

Gamma2 immunostaining is shown in RGLs, but Supplementary Figure 2f electrophysiology tests GFP-positive neurons at thirty days, not RGLs. Its seven-of-ten cKO response pattern is not a measured RGL deletion efficiency. Recombination can persist in descendants, so later survival or differentiation may contribute to clone composition.

Thirty-day Figure 3f and Supplementary Figure 3e use incompletely reconciled clone denominators: the supplementary pie categories omit single-R and no-R classes. N includes intermediate progenitors or neurons, not exclusively mature neurons. Exact class percentages must not be pooled or converted to transition probabilities.

The population diazepam protocol is 5 mg/kg intraperitoneally once daily for five days. The clonal drug comparison instead uses six daily doses after tamoxifen and analysis at seven days. Diazepam is systemic. Pairwise drug responses or nulls without a reported genotype-by-drug interaction do not isolate an exclusive cell-autonomous mediator.

Social isolation starts immediately after weaning and lasts at least six weeks before labeling. The two housing conditions are crossed with light versus sham; this is not a selective learning manipulation. PV activity and extracellular GABA are not measured as the intervening response to isolation in the same animals.

Figure 5c retains higher EdU-positive RGL density in isolated versus group-housed animals under PV light stimulation (reported P < 0.05). In that same housing comparison, MCM2-positive density and fraction are nonsignificant (P > 0.1). These endpoints do not support complete abolition of the isolation effect or equivalence; the light-treated group is also distinct from the untreated group-housed baseline.

Figure 4 population comparisons use three or four animals per condition; Figure 5c uses four. Reported Student t-tests do not provide an equivalence margin, complete unit manifest or a formal factorial interaction. SST/VIP nulls apply to the tested lines, protocols and readouts, not all possible interneuron functions.

No matched experiment follows physiological circuit demand through PV signaling, RGL division, newborn-neuron survival and functional integration to restoration of circuit output. Supplementary Figure 8 imports schematic connectivity proportions, not measured weights. A reported reconstruction covering over 200 RGLs is spatial coverage, not 200 verified functional contacts or a minimum carrier count. Movie legends were read; movie files and custom reconstruction code were not replayed.

All six main PDF pages, Figures 1-5, Online Methods and all nine supplementary PDF pages with Figures 1-8 and Movie 1-3 legends were reviewed. Raw animal-level data, microscopy, recordings, movie files and analysis code were not obtained or independently reproduced.

contexts.correctionCheck: PubMed metadata, the author-hosted full text and DOI-specific notice searches were checked. No correction resolving the specified source conflicts was identified; this is not exhaustive correction surveillance.
contexts.finding: PF sample selectivity can reappear between distractors, while match enhancement and repetition suppression have different task dependence. These observations do not establish a causal local storage or PF-to-IT route.
limitations: Two rhesus monkeys supplied 264 screened PF units; 145 task-responsive units were retained (98 in the ABBA-trained animal and 47 in the standard-task animal). The other 109 units were not studied further. Cells are nested within two animals; this is not an unbiased PF prevalence estimate. Sex and ages are unspecified.

The sample and test images last 500 ms with 1000-ms blank intervals and zero to four intervening nonmatches. ABBA trials repeat an irrelevant nonmatch; standard trials do not. Task/training differences are confounded with animal identity. PF visual responses use 90-290 ms after onset and delay activity the last 600 ms of each blank interval.

The text reports forty delay-selective units, including 33/98 ABBA and 7/47 standard units; Table 1 instead lists 32/98 for ABBA. Match-enhancement counts also differ across the text and table, with mixed response types. No exact reconciled subgroup prevalence or exclusive partition is admitted.

The 135 IT units were previously recorded in the ABBA animal and reanalyzed. They are not simultaneous paired PF-IT recordings or an independent replication. Figure 7 pools forty PF units across two animals against twenty-five IT units from one animal; selection and animal composition differ.

Best/worst-sample traces use selected neurons and sample rankings. Reported half-trial discriminant classification excludes the first delay and averages 20.8% versus six-way chance of 16.7%; the paper does not specify that unit selection was nested within training folds. No classification, multiplicity correction or neural minimum is independently reproduced.

PF feedback to IT is proposed in the Discussion. The authors explicitly state that the direct PF-deactivation test of IT match enhancement had not been tried. Response precedence, delay persistence and ramping do not identify an exclusive local recurrence, directed feedback route, accumulator or complete control circuit.

contexts.correctionCheck: PubMed metadata, the author-hosted full text and DOI-specific notice searches were checked. No correction resolving the specified source conflicts was identified; this is not exhaustive correction surveillance.
contexts.finding: Unattended-category decoding transiently exceeds chance after the pulse; global source metrics show no significant attention-state effects.
limitations: Category classifiers distinguish face, word and motion information. Above-chance category evidence does not demonstrate recovery of the particular remembered item. Below-chance-threshold evidence is not absence of all neuronal activity; fMRI and EEG are different readouts.

The supplementary protocol gives different initial delays across experiments (7, 5 and 2 seconds), whereas Figure 1 supplies a generic timeline. TMS timing is measured after cue offset: 2.5 seconds in Experiments 2 and 4, and 2-3 seconds with jitter in Experiment 3. One schematic is not a common exact trial manifest.

EEG features undergo 2.5-second centered temporal smoothing. This mixes past and future samples and does not establish precise millisecond reactivation latency. All-trial normalization and trial-level cross-validation do not provide a held-out-person generalization estimate. The stated 191 training trials fits Experiment 3 but does not transparently describe the 164-trial Experiment 2 sessions.

TMS occurs on every EEG trial. State/category comparisons do not substitute for sham or no-TMS trials within the same EEG preparation. Modeled cortical fields, scalp targets and source-inversion meshes are not measured synaptic connections. Neither synaptic weights nor an exclusive silent storage carrier was directly measured.

Main text, all four main figures, the complete supplementary scientific text, all six supplementary figures and Table S1 were reviewed. Raw trials, participant allocation records, custom code and Movie S1 were not reproduced. Inconsistent figure cross-references are resolved only to visibly identified panels, not by inventing missing results.

Nine initial MRI participants yielded six completing participants after separate exclusions/dropout. Eighteen sessions of 164 trials yield 2952 trials; the reported t(17) uses sessions, not eighteen independent people. Targeted and nontargeted conditions both exceed chance; differing significance levels or Bayes factors do not establish a direct target-condition difference.

Supplementary beta-band decoding concerns analysis features, not a frequency-specific intervention demonstrating a necessary beta oscillator. Global-metric nulls are not equivalence tests or proof that all geometry is uninformative.

contexts.finding: PF sample selectivity can reappear between distractors, while match enhancement and repetition suppression have different task dependence. These observations do not establish a causal local storage or PF-to-IT route.
limitations: Two rhesus monkeys supplied 264 screened PF units; 145 task-responsive units were retained (98 in the ABBA-trained animal and 47 in the standard-task animal). The other 109 units were not studied further. Cells are nested within two animals; this is not an unbiased PF prevalence estimate. Sex and ages are unspecified.

The sample and test images last 500 ms with 1000-ms blank intervals and zero to four intervening nonmatches. ABBA trials repeat an irrelevant nonmatch; standard trials do not. Task/training differences are confounded with animal identity. PF visual responses use 90-290 ms after onset and delay activity the last 600 ms of each blank interval.

The text reports forty delay-selective units, including 33/98 ABBA and 7/47 standard units; Table 1 instead lists 32/98 for ABBA. Match-enhancement counts also differ across the text and table, with mixed response types. No exact reconciled subgroup prevalence or exclusive partition is admitted.

The 135 IT units were previously recorded in the ABBA animal and reanalyzed. They are not simultaneous paired PF-IT recordings or an independent replication. Figure 7 pools forty PF units across two animals against twenty-five IT units from one animal; selection and animal composition differ.

Best/worst-sample traces use selected neurons and sample rankings. Reported half-trial discriminant classification excludes the first delay and averages 20.8% versus six-way chance of 16.7%; the paper does not specify that unit selection was nested within training folds. No classification, multiplicity correction or neural minimum is independently reproduced.

PF feedback to IT is proposed in the Discussion. The authors explicitly state that the direct PF-deactivation test of IT match enhancement had not been tried. Response precedence, delay persistence and ramping do not identify an exclusive local recurrence, directed feedback route, accumulator or complete control circuit.

contexts.correctionCheck: The versioned arXiv author report was read. Publisher bytes, exhaustive later corrections and upstream calibration experiments were not independently reviewed.
contexts.finding: Equation 19 reports 29.164705(55) MHz/T conditional on Equation 2, rather than a reference-free absolute moment.
limitations: The fitted frequencies and the admitted ratio are positive magnitudes. The opposite signed neutron and 199Hg gyromagnetic ratios are assumptions in the Earth-rotation correction; the positive ratio is not an independent determination of those signs or of a signed neutron moment in nuclear magnetons.

The 199Hg atomic response 7.590118(13) MHz/T is adopted from Equation 2, which quotes an external Hg-to-shielded-proton-in-water calibration and reference value. The upstream Cagnac experiment and fundamental-constant adjustment are not reviewed or reproduced here. This is not the moment of an isolated bare Hg nucleus or a new absolute calibration from the PSI counts.

The neutron frequency-per-field magnitude is conditional on the adopted Hg atomic reference. The positive product does not determine a signed magnetic moment, a new nuclear-magneton conversion or a constituent count. The later free-proton trap result is not substituted for the shielded-proton-in-water reference.

Equation 20 instead combines the same ratio with an adopted neutron value to infer Hg. Substituting that inferred Hg back into the ratio returns the adopted neutron input; these alternative calibrations cannot be counted as independent confirmations of each other.
This spin-precession result supplies no neutron electric or magnetic form factor, free-neutron survival estimate, bound-neutron stability, hadronization mechanism or universal construction rule.

contexts.correctionCheck: Identity and publication type were checked against the primary title page and institution record. Reviewed printed arithmetic, formula and campaign-date conflicts remain explicit; no exhaustive later correction or independent experimental replication review is claimed.
contexts.finding: The formal witness and printed calculations separate consistent identities, rounded-input agreement and unreconciled source conflicts without reproducing the experimental calibration.
contexts.journal: University of Tennessee, Knoxville doctoral dissertation
limitations: The ideal transfer identity uses R_Pu=r_Pu,stack/Omega_stack, Omega_AG=r_Pu,AG/R_Pu and R_n=r_gamma,thick*r_alpha,thin/(r_gamma,thin*Omega_AG). The boron gamma branching fraction and thin-target absorption normalization cancel only with the stated common detector response and loss corrections. Omega here is a fraction of 4*pi; illuminated alpha-detector area is assumed fully efficient. R_Pu denotes total alpha emission from the source, including its minor 240Pu/241Am contributions, not a separately isolated pure-239Pu decay rate.

The thesis uses two spacer configurations and the Cu-Cu-1 aperture, diameter 25.6725+/-0.0030 mm. The 2018 article reports a nickel-coated copper aperture of 25.765192+/-0.000240 mm and source distance 87.4226+/-0.0015 mm, with different alpha rates and activity. Their reported source calibrations cannot be substituted or averaged as independent determinations of an identically specified preparation. No cross-version correction or physical source-aging estimate is established.

The thesis separates uncorrelated stacking/counting errors from a common aperture error. Body page 92 gives 0.023 percent, while Appendix B page 150 prints a correlated fraction of 2.3e-5. The latter differs by a factor of ten. Both printed scenarios remain explicit; the body convention reproduces the reported total uncertainty to displayed precision, without establishing which unrounded inputs or implementation were used.

The printed thesis stack estimates 23543.9+/-8.4 and 23545.6+/-5.2 per second give a weighted mean of 23545.129016... per second and uncorrelated uncertainty 4.421378... per second. That central calculation rounds to 23545.1, not the reported 23545.2. A conservative box for rounding of the printed inputs permits values rounding to the reported mean; it does not recover the original digits or prove their values.

The 2018 article reports the corrected alpha count rate 125.740 per second and effective Omega_stack=0.0053415, followed by R_Pu=23538.4 per second. Their printed central quotient is 23540.204... per second, and display-rounding intervals do not include the reported activity center. Additional input or correction reconciliation is unresolved. This is a failure to reconstruct the printed result from those displayed inputs, not evidence that the experimental numerical analysis is wrong.

Equation 28 in the 2018 article omits the factor 1/2 required to invert Equation 12, which counts both alpha and triton products. Equation 26 defines phi_abs as an absorbed fraction near 0.01016, but the later text labels the transmission correction 0.989846 as phi_abs. Omega here is a fraction of 4*pi; illuminated alpha-detector area is assumed fully efficient. R_Pu denotes total alpha emission from the source, including its minor 240Pu/241Am contributions, not a separately isolated pure-239Pu decay rate.

The beam analysis uses timed beam-on minus beam-off rates, the geometric mean of top and bottom gamma-detector rates, and thin-target/thick-target/thin-target cycles to suppress first-order gamma-efficiency drift. Gamma backgrounds, thresholds, pulse pileup, dead time and silicon-capture contributions remain explicit corrections; a count-rate ratio is not a raw absolute neutron count.

Cancellation of nuclear normalization inputs in the ideal rate identity does not eliminate nuclear data from every correction. The detailed article uses neutron scattering/absorption inputs, radiative-capture cross sections, material attenuation and modeled neutron/gamma transport. Its remaining upstream nuclear data, image records and simulation implementations are not independently reproduced.

Alpha-source activity, monitor count efficiency and a neutron-decay lifetime are different quantities. None establishes nucleon formation, eternal proton stability, a universal constituent minimum or a unique explanation of beam/bottle differences.

contexts.correctionCheck: Final author version v2 and journal identity checked. This is a historical result; later overlapping analyses, all upstream corrections and an exhaustive correction search are not claimed.
contexts.finding: The reanalysed 7 TeV and new 8 TeV four-lepton selections give the Figure 2 invariant-mass spectrum. In the Table 3 window 120-130 GeV, the reported observed counts are 6 four-muon, 5 mixed-electron/muon and 2 four-electron candidates; modeled signal and backgrounds are separate.
limitations: The 2011 7 TeV and April-June 2012 8 TeV samples are distinct exposures. Reanalysed 2011 channels, their earlier publications and the combined result reuse data and are not independent replications. Luminosities are channel-dependent, and plotted categories are not additional experiments.

Reconstruction and energy/momentum calibration use simulation and W, Z, J/psi and other control data. Background control regions and theoretical signal templates are required inputs. These controls are not independent Higgs discoveries; their raw data, transfer factors and full response are not reproduced.

The four-lepton invariant mass follows particle selection and a Z-mass constraint on the leading pair in this low-mass region. Table 3 gives candidates within 120-130 GeV, not identified Higgs counts. Figure 1 is a relaxed-background selection; Figures 2-3 and the fitted result reuse the selected sample.

The 23788/35251 counts cover 100-160 GeV before signal/background separation. Ten categories per energy have different response and purity. Figure 4 weighted panels use ln(1+S/B) from the model and fitted background and show the same events, not new measurements; the actual search uses the category likelihoods.

The 8 TeV analysis uses only e-mu/mu-e final states and missing transverse momentum. Table 5 counts impose an additional 0.75*mH<mT<mH window at mH=125 GeV. The likelihood instead uses five mT bins for 0 jets, three for 1 jet and an mT-integrated 2-jet contribution without that final window; Figure 6 and Table 5 cannot be substituted for one another. Missing neutrinos prevent a fully reconstructed invariant-mass peak.

contexts.correctionCheck: Final author version v2 and journal identity checked. This is a historical result; later overlapping analyses, all upstream corrections and an exhaustive correction search are not claimed.
contexts.finding: The full published combination reports local significance 5.9 standard deviations (p0=1.7e-9), and global significance about 5.1 (p0=1.7e-7) over 110-600 GeV. At mH=126 GeV the fitted common signal strength relative to the Standard Model is 1.4 +/-0.3.
limitations: Table 6 includes imported 7 TeV WW, tau, associated bb and high-mass ZZ/WW analyses in addition to the updated four-lepton/diphoton and new 8 TeV channels. Only this article account of those imported likelihood inputs is reviewed; their earlier analysis papers are not independently replayed. Correlated nuisance parameters prevent treating displayed channel results as independent numerical replicas.

The 126.0 +/-0.4 statistical +/-0.4 systematic GeV mass uses only the four-lepton and diphoton channels, allowing their signal strengths to vary independently. This fitted mass is distinct from the 126.5 GeV hypothesis maximizing the local excess and from the broader combined signal-strength fit.

Table 7 gives 6.0 local standard deviations before the additional photon/electron energy-scale and resolution treatment described in Section 9.2 reduces it to 5.9. The reported global 5.1 uses the 110-600 GeV search range. These are likelihood/background-tail results, not posterior Higgs probabilities, and no local verifier reproduces them.

Reconstruction and energy/momentum calibration use simulation and W, Z, J/psi and other control data. Background control regions and theoretical signal templates are required inputs. These controls are not independent Higgs discoveries; their raw data, transfer factors and full response are not reproduced.

The historical observation is compatible with the Standard Model Higgs hypothesis and disfavors spin one through the diphoton channel. It is not by itself a unique spin-parity, every-Yukawa, Higgs-potential, W/Z-width or vacuum-stability determination. Later data are not imported into this 2012 result.
contexts.observable: Original same-acquisition mass, signal-strength and background-tail inference under the published response/nuisance model.
contexts.preparation: Profile the stated signal/background likelihood with correlated nuisance parameters. Diphotons use unbinned category likelihoods; WW uses transverse-mass bins for 0/1 jet and an integrated 2-jet contribution. The full Table 6 combination also imports earlier 7 TeV channels, while the mass fit selects the four-lepton and diphoton channels only.

contexts.correctionCheck: Final author version v2 and journal identity checked. This is a historical result; later overlapping analyses, all upstream corrections and an exhaustive correction search are not claimed.
contexts.finding: The reanalysed 7 TeV and new 8 TeV four-lepton selections give the Figure 2 invariant-mass spectrum. In the Table 3 window 120-130 GeV, the reported observed counts are 6 four-muon, 5 mixed-electron/muon and 2 four-electron candidates; modeled signal and backgrounds are separate.
limitations: The 2011 7 TeV and April-June 2012 8 TeV samples are distinct exposures. Reanalysed 2011 channels, their earlier publications and the combined result reuse data and are not independent replications. Luminosities are channel-dependent, and plotted categories are not additional experiments.

Reconstruction and energy/momentum calibration use simulation and W, Z, J/psi and other control data. Background control regions and theoretical signal templates are required inputs. These controls are not independent Higgs discoveries; their raw data, transfer factors and full response are not reproduced.

The four-lepton invariant mass follows particle selection and a Z-mass constraint on the leading pair in this low-mass region. Table 3 gives candidates within 120-130 GeV, not identified Higgs counts. Figure 1 is a relaxed-background selection; Figures 2-3 and the fitted result reuse the selected sample.

The 23788/35251 counts cover 100-160 GeV before signal/background separation. Ten categories per energy have different response and purity. Figure 4 weighted panels use ln(1+S/B) from the model and fitted background and show the same events, not new measurements; the actual search uses the category likelihoods.

The 8 TeV analysis uses only e-mu/mu-e final states and missing transverse momentum. Table 5 counts impose an additional 0.75*mH<mT<mH window at mH=125 GeV. The likelihood instead uses five mT bins for 0 jets, three for 1 jet and an mT-integrated 2-jet contribution without that final window; Figure 6 and Table 5 cannot be substituted for one another. Missing neutrinos prevent a fully reconstructed invariant-mass peak.
contexts.observable: Selected reconstructed lepton/photon and transverse-mass samples, including their explicit plotting/selection boundaries.
contexts.preparation: Use the ATLAS pp data at 7 TeV in 2011 and 8 TeV in April-June 2012, with channel luminosities 4.6-4.8 and 5.8-5.9 fb^-1. Apply channel-specific lepton/photon triggers, object reconstruction, isolation, jet and missing-momentum selections.

limitations: The 1994 result is a global least-squares solution of twenty pairwise comparisons. Its covariance matrix determines uncertainties of correlated atomic masses and mass differences; the short article does not provide that matrix or every input ratio.
For a mass difference, Var(D-H)=Var(D)+Var(H)-2*Cov(D,H). Adding printed marginal errors in quadrature assumes zero covariance and is not a reconstruction of the published fit.

The authors report reduced chi-square 0.74 and redundant routes to the mass table. These internal checks constrain the stated error model; they do not logically exclude every possible common systematic.

The quoted 2.6e-10 relative rms magnetic fluctuation applies to a single frequency measurement in the 1994 analysis. A typical one-night ratio error near 1e-10 and the final fitted mass uncertainties have different averaging domains.

The 1993 treatment describes approximately Gaussian residuals for its example; the 1994 robust estimator downweights non-Gaussian outliers. These are different analysis descriptions, not interchangeable procedures.
The carbon-12 neutral-atom reference has mass exactly 12 u by definition. A carbon ion differs by electron mass and ionization energy; treating C+ as exactly 12 u is incorrect.

Converting molecular-ion comparisons to neutral isolated ground-state atoms requires electron, chemical-binding and ionization-energy terms. The 1994 analysis uses ideal-gas heats of formation at 0 K; this is not the trap temperature.

contexts.correctionCheck: Author v2 and publisher identity checked; journal publication is 28 June 2005. The reviewed v2 includes corrected Table I uncertainties. contexts.finding: The two-state fit gives an avoided crossing, with the lower energy approaching the two-static-light-meson threshold over the measured range. A quadratic gap fit reports r_c/a=15.00(8) and a*DeltaE_c=0.0217(9); physical-unit conversion and uncertainties retain their declared scale and ensemble.
limitations: One lattice spacing and one sea-quark mass are studied; these are not physical up/down masses or a two-plus-one-flavor ensemble. Finite-volume diagnostics are not an infinite-volume or continuum extrapolation.

Quark-propagator matrix entries use 20 thermalized configurations separated by 125 HMC trajectories. Wilson loops use 184 configurations separated by 25 trajectories and aligned into 20 bins; the two sample counts are correlated, not independent replications.

Smearing, a modified static action, low-mode eigenvectors and residual stochastic estimators improve overlap and noise. Low-mode truncation alone is biased; finite stochastic estimates are not exact propagators.
Monte Carlo sampling and Euclidean separation are not real-time string formation. No underlying configuration stream, correlator covariance or independent numerical fit is available in this graph.

The correlation matrix retains Q-Q, Q-B and B-B entries, with disconnected and connected two-meson terms and their flavor factors. The I=1 disconnected comparison is a sector of the same dynamical ensemble, not a separate quenched simulation.
The Wilson-loop-only readout at r greater than r_c and measured Euclidean times t<=9a shows no visible string-breaking signal. This is a sensitivity limitation of that operator and time window.
The null readout does not negate mixing inferred from the full correlation matrix or demonstrate the existence of isolated free quarks.
The energy-spectrum and mixing fits share this ensemble; no independent replication or intervention switching off sea quarks is supplied.
Fit the common 2 x 2 correlation matrix with five parameters theta, a_Q, a_B, E1 and E2, retaining the separation-dependent time windows in Equations 71-75 and the two-state truncation.
Divide matrix correlators by the squared static-light correlator to infer E1-2m_B and E2-2m_B. Static self-energies cancel in these differences; absolute static energies are cutoff-dependent.

The lower fitted energy approaches the two-meson threshold within the sampled separation range. A Cornell fit below the breaking region is not a linearly rising ground-state potential at all distances.

The quadratic gap fit uses 14a<=r_bar<=16a and reports r_c/a=15.00(8), a*DeltaE_c=0.0217(9), r_c/r0=2.496(26), r_c=1.248(13) fm and DeltaE_c=51(3) MeV with r0=0.5 fm. Quoted errors are statistical; scale-setting, sea-mass and continuum uncertainties are not included.
Figure 17's no-mixing comparison uses operator sectors from the same two-flavor ensemble. It is not a separately sampled quenched control or an intervention experiment.

Figure 22's two-plus-one-flavor bands are explicitly speculative. The finite-window parametrization has an incorrect large-distance asymptote; neither supplies a physical-mass calculation or universal string-breaking threshold.
In the declared two-state basis, g(r)=DeltaE(r)*sin(2*theta(r))/2 has units of energy. It is a mixing coupling and Euclidean relaxation quantity, not a measured stochastic real-time decay rate.
Use the Equation 77 basis convention. The summary sine/cosine swap and the Equation 85 equal-mixing mismatch remain unresolved source inconsistencies; an exact theta(r_c)=pi/4 is not assumed.
The Equation 96 consistency ratio reuses correlators and the fitted energy gap. Agreement is not independent replication; small-separation corrections limit its plateau.
Finite-mass quarkonium, irreversible hadronization, stable nuclear or atomic organization and a downward causal rule are not computed. A static spectral description does not establish those claims.
Use Equation 77: |1>=cos(theta)|Q>+sin(theta)|B>, and Equation 78: |2>=-sin(theta)|Q>+cos(theta)|B>. The Section VII summary interchanges sine and cosine and is not the adopted convention.
The two-state truncation omits higher excitations. Mixing angles depend on the selected basis; fitted source overlaps are not probabilities of an exhaustive Fock decomposition.

The gap minimum defines r_c. Equation 85 gives theta(r_s)=pi/2-c*pi/4, so the text's exact theta(r_s)=pi/4 identity does not hold for fitted c=0.914. No exact identification of r_s, r_c and equal mixing is admitted.
The Euclidean transfer description concerns energy levels. A real-time decay, irreversible hadronization or downward change to quark dynamics requires additional dynamics and evidence.

The energy-spectrum and mixing fits share this ensemble; no independent replication or intervention switching off sea quarks is supplied.
Fit the common 2 x 2 correlation matrix with five parameters theta, a_Q, a_B, E1 and E2, retaining the separation-dependent time windows in Equations 71-75 and the two-state truncation.
Divide matrix correlators by the squared static-light correlator to infer E1-2m_B and E2-2m_B. Static self-energies cancel in these differences; absolute static energies are cutoff-dependent.

The lower fitted energy approaches the two-meson threshold within the sampled separation range. A Cornell fit below the breaking region is not a linearly rising ground-state potential at all distances.

The quadratic gap fit uses 14a<=r_bar<=16a and reports r_c/a=15.00(8), a*DeltaE_c=0.0217(9), r_c/r0=2.496(26), r_c=1.248(13) fm and DeltaE_c=51(3) MeV with r0=0.5 fm. Quoted errors are statistical; scale-setting, sea-mass and continuum uncertainties are not included.
Figure 17's no-mixing comparison uses operator sectors from the same two-flavor ensemble. It is not a separately sampled quenched control or an intervention experiment.

Figure 22's two-plus-one-flavor bands are explicitly speculative. The finite-window parametrization has an incorrect large-distance asymptote; neither supplies a physical-mass calculation or universal string-breaking threshold.
In the declared two-state basis, g(r)=DeltaE(r)*sin(2*theta(r))/2 has units of energy. It is a mixing coupling and Euclidean relaxation quantity, not a measured stochastic real-time decay rate.
Use the Equation 77 basis convention. The summary sine/cosine swap and the Equation 85 equal-mixing mismatch remain unresolved source inconsistencies; an exact theta(r_c)=pi/4 is not assumed.
The Equation 96 consistency ratio reuses correlators and the fitted energy gap. Agreement is not independent replication; small-separation corrections limit its plateau.
Finite-mass quarkonium, irreversible hadronization, stable nuclear or atomic organization and a downward causal rule are not computed. A static spectral description does not establish those claims.
Use Equation 77: |1>=cos(theta)|Q>+sin(theta)|B>, and Equation 78: |2>=-sin(theta)|Q>+cos(theta)|B>. The Section VII summary interchanges sine and cosine and is not the adopted convention.
The two-state truncation omits higher excitations. Mixing angles depend on the selected basis; fitted source overlaps are not probabilities of an exhaustive Fock decomposition.

The gap minimum defines r_c. Equation 85 gives theta(r_s)=pi/2-c*pi/4, so the text's exact theta(r_s)=pi/4 identity does not hold for fitted c=0.914. No exact identification of r_s, r_c and equal mixing is admitted.
The Euclidean transfer description concerns energy levels. A real-time decay, irreversible hadronization or downward change to quark dynamics requires additional dynamics and evidence.

These are an approximate comparison hypothesis, not a modern fitted mass prediction or a measurement of Omega spin/parity.
The reported 0.7e-10 s is the reconstructed proper decay time of this event, not an ensemble mean lifetime or a lifetime fit. Neither a branching fraction nor all-channel stability follows.

contexts.finding: The report conditionally identifies particle 3 with Omega- from Q=-1, inferred S=-3 and reconstructed mass 1686 +/- 12 MeV/c^2, with a production missing mass of 500 +/- 25 MeV/c^2 compatible with K0. The quoted event proper decay time is 0.7e-10 s; no spin/parity or ensemble-lifetime determination is supplied.
limitations: The cascade hypothesis is K-+p -> Omega-+K++K0, followed by Omega- -> Xi0+pi-, Xi0 -> Lambda0+pi0, Lambda0 -> p+pi- and pi0 -> gamma+gamma with photon conversions. The Lambda fit, photon pairing, transverse balance and missing-mass checks share this event; they are not independent replications.

Strangeness -3 is inferred using the reconstructed Xi0 channel, the weak-decay Delta S=1 assumption and competing-channel reasoning. Charge and mass support a conditional Omega identification; the one-event evidence does not measure J^P=3/2+ or establish the full decuplet dynamics.

Barnes adopts the decuplet expectation I=0, Q=-1, S=-3, J^P=3/2+ and mass about 1680 MeV/c^2. Figure 1 uses historical centers 1238,1385,1532; their arithmetic continuation is 1679. These are an approximate comparison hypothesis, not a modern fitted mass prediction or a measurement of Omega spin/parity.
The reported 0.7e-10 s is the reconstructed proper decay time of this event, not an ensemble mean lifetime or a lifetime fit. Neither a branching fraction nor all-channel stability follows.

The report gives 1686 +/- 12 MeV/c^2 while explicitly deferring a detailed mass discussion until more events and better-understood systematic errors. No new confidence-level meaning, independent significance, modern mass combination or numerical reconstruction of that uncertainty is assigned.

The report presents one selected event from partially analyzed pictures. Approximately 100000 photographs and 10^6 feet of kaon tracks are exposure descriptions, not Omega counts or a measured production rate. The archive stamp and publication date do not establish an acquisition date range.

source.title: Measurement of the neutron lifetime by counting trapped protons in a cold neutron beam

limitations: The measured beam observable is a proton-producing decay rate relative to the monitored neutron population in the trapping region. Identifying its inverse with the total free-neutron lifetime requires the stated decay-channel and detection assumptions. Storage disappearance and proton counting are distinct observables; no branching fraction or explanation of their difference is inferred here.

Cancellation of the neutron velocity distribution assumes a thin monitor with inverse-velocity response and unchanged beam between the trap and monitor. Finite absorption, spatial profiles, scattering and beam transport still require the original corrections.

The effective trap length is L=n*l+L_end. A fit of the proton-to-monitor count-rate ratio versus electrode number removes a constant end contribution only under the common-end-region assumption; the paper separately corrects nonlinearity from field, geometry and beam divergence. Proton trapping for milliseconds is not neutron storage for a lifetime.

The neutron-lifetime results do not establish neutron formation, proton stability, a universal constituent minimum or a present-day beam/bottle discrepancy. The 2013 historical world averages are not admitted without review of their components.
rationale.scope: The Nico 2000-2001 proton-counting beam acquisition, its published 2005 lifetime and the Yue 2011 monitor calibration applied in 2013 to the same acquisition.

description: Fit the reconstructed-length distribution with an exponential convolved with Equation 3 resolution plus fixed MC background shapes and normalizations. Float the signal normalization, exponential scale and five resolution parameters; fix asymmetry A=2.5 cm^-1. Calibrate the fitted scale with generated mean lengths 84, 87.11 and 90 micrometers. Apply the reported alignment, fixed-asymmetry, beam/radiation, fit-range, background and adopted-mass uncertainties before quoting the combined lifetime.
name: Belle tau-lifetime fit and calibration
openObligations: The source supplies a distribution fit and MC calibration, not a locally reproduced likelihood or covariance. Its fitted resolution asymmetry is fixed because of its lifetime correlation; simulated background yields/shapes remain model inputs.
The source uses length units for the fit variable and scale. Table I systematic errors are in micrometers; the reported total 0.101 micrometers is rounded to 0.10 in the final c*tau result.

review.limit: The released ratios are a fitted-normalization data product, with spline-derived error scaling; they are not a temporally prior independent input to that same fit. The cross-section ratios already incorporate acceptance and radiation modeling, Feshbach Coulomb correction and spline-fit normalization. They are not raw counts or independently measured absolute Born cross sections. Standard-dipole normalization is a model input. The 31 normalization parameters enter shared products. Equation 48 multiplies data and error by their product; ancillary Section 4 uses the reciprocal nuisance-parameter convention on the model. Their numerical parameter values are not interchangeable. Column 6 contains already-scaled point-to-point errors, not counting errors to scale a second time. The 315-MeV acquisition uses the current-based luminosity estimate after a monitor-setting problem. Kinematics must use the acceptance-averaged Q^2 and beam energy, not the central spectrometer angle. Multiplying columns 5-8 by column 9 undoes the applied Coulomb correction. Columns 12-18 change model normalization; the systematic variations in column 10 require new fits, not new observations.

limitations: The 2014 author report describes the August 2006, November 2006 and May 2007 MAMI acquisition previously reported in 2010. The 2010 and 2014 publications, spline fits and Rosenbluth separation are dependent uses of this acquisition, not independent replications.

Unpolarized elastic scattering in the ultrarelativistic one-photon approximation determines epsilon*GE^2+tau*GM^2. Signs require normalization and continuity conventions. GE(0)=1 and GM(0)=mu_p are imposed reference values; this is not a new magnetic-moment measurement, a count of constituents or a formation law.

The released ratios are a fitted-normalization data product, with spline-derived error scaling; they are not a temporally prior independent input to that same fit. The cross-section ratios already incorporate acceptance and radiation modeling, Feshbach Coulomb correction and spline-fit normalization. They are not raw counts or independently measured absolute Born cross sections. Standard-dipole normalization is a model input.

The 31 normalization parameters enter shared products. Equation 48 multiplies data and error by their product; ancillary Section 4 uses the reciprocal nuisance-parameter convention on the model. Their numerical parameter values are not interchangeable. Column 6 contains already-scaled point-to-point errors, not counting errors to scale a second time. The 315-MeV acquisition uses the current-based luminosity estimate after a monitor-setting problem.

Kinematics must use the acceptance-averaged Q^2 and beam energy, not the central spectrometer angle. Multiplying columns 5-8 by column 9 undoes the applied Coulomb correction. Columns 12-18 change model normalization; the systematic variations in column 10 require new fits, not new observations.

The selected Mainz-only spline table tabulates GE, GM/mu_p and mu_p*GE/GM, with separate statistical, experimental systematic and Coulomb-variation columns. Its 1000 grid values are evaluations of one fit, not 1000 new measurements.

The fit errors describe 68 percent pointwise bands. They are not simultaneous bands, independent draws or the full covariance. The Coulomb-variation band varies a correction by 50 percent; it is not an independent Gaussian error to combine without a model.

The Mainz-only analysis applies Feshbach Coulomb correction but not a complete hard two-photon-exchange treatment. Limited epsilon coverage weakens GE/GM separation above Q^2 about 0.55 GeV^2; the single-energy endpoint does not separately identify both form factors without the fit model.

Sachs form factors describe elastic current response in a specified framework. A static three-dimensional charge-density interpretation is frame dependent; no literal three-quark geometry, unique pion-cloud mechanism, neutron form factor, hadronization dynamics or nuclear stability follows.
